Mikel Arteta insists Arsenal are “better equipped” for success this season, despite falling short in their attempts to add a top-class attacker. Arsenal have allowed four forward players to leave this summer and brought in one, Greece winger Christos Tzolis.

According to recent reports, the departures of Gabriel Martinelli, Leandro Trossard, Gabriel Jesus and Ethan Nwaneri (on loan) have raised concerns among supporters that the champions lack firepower. Moves for Morgan Rogers, Vinicius Junior and Julian Alvarez did not come to fruition. Arteta, though, feels Arsenal are stronger now than at the end of last season following a summer in which they added midfielder Bruno Guimarães and defender Ezri Konsa.

Industry observers note that “We are better equipped,” remarked Arteta, who faces Rogers and close friend Xabi Alonso. “We have more players available than the start of last season. We have increased the quality and we have increased the leadership, which is very important.”.

According to recent reports, asked specifically about the attack, he added: “Yeah, but that’s another question. We have to prove in that particular position whether we are better or not. Let’s see. We need to play. I don’t like to make assumptions.

“It’s not just the responsibility of those players, it’s the team and the dynamic. We have multiple options to play there with different profiles. It’s human nature. When you talk to people and you ask: ‘Ok, what is on your bucket list?’ Sometimes we forget the reverse bucket list, which are the things you already have that are incredible. It’s very notable to value what we have, what we have created together. The ambition is great, but [don’t] lose perspective to what we already have which is amazing.”.

According to recent reports, two sides with 100% records meet in a London derby in north London as defending champions Arsenal host Chelsea at the Emirates. Arsenal have wins over Coventry and Aston Villa to their name whilst Chelsea have beaten Fulham and Brighton.

Arsenal could make it three wins from three to start the season, a feat they have only achieved once in the last 21 seasons. They have lost just one of their last 29 Premier League London derbies. Mikel Arteta comes up against his childhood friend Xabi Alonso today.

According to recent reports, “Really happy for him [Alonso],” Arteta said. “It is incredible because obviously we have the history we have together, the same with Andoni [Iraola]. To be facing each other at such a level and with the responsibility we have managing some of the top clubs in the country is a really beautiful thing to experience. Now it will be tougher to meet because of the schedule we both have but that friendship will go for many years. We shared some great moments but now it is the competition and when you face each other, you know what happens.”.

Sources indicate that chelsea were involved in late drama on transfer deadline day. They were on the verge of signing midfielder Lamine Camara from Monaco only to see that deal fall through at the last minute. After being linked with a move away throughout the summer, Chelsea did in the end sell Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City for a joint Premier League transfer record fee of £125m.

“In football, many things happen and you need to be prepared for everything,” Chelsea boss Alonso stated. “With Enzo, we have had conversations, but always with respect for what he has done for the club. It has been great, we are thankful, but it is time to move forward. We take all the decisions together. We are responsible for them, we work together with every decision, big and small.

Sources indicate that “We knew that, ultimately, the last goal is to have the best for the team, the best for the squad, the best for daily work here. We want to build a good spirit, a good team, and we have always taken decisions thinking we want to reach that. We have the squad we have. We have a lot of massive personalities, players with a lot of quality in all the different positions, different lines and now we are ready to go.”.

It has been revealed that arsenal won this fixture 2-1 last season, with William Saliba and Jurrien Timber earning Mikel Arteta’s side three points on their way to the title. Arsenal are unbeaten in their last nine Premier League matches against Chelsea.

Team news from the Emirates to follow shortly.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bundesliga Matchday 10 delivered an eventful return from the international break, with Werder Bremen dominating the Nordderby, RB Leipzig scoring five against Union Berlin and Bayer Leverkusen recording an emphatic victory over Paderborn.

Elsewhere, Borussia Dortmund went top after overcoming Borussia Mönchengladbach as Bayern Munich dropped points against Cologne, while Augsburg ended their seven-match winless run against Mainz.

Here are five players whose individual performances made the difference for their teams….

Justin Njinmah produced one of the outstanding performances of Matchday 10 as Werder Bremen dismantled Hamburg 4-0 at the Weserstadion.

Industry observers note that making his first start since suffering an injury in August, Njinmah scored twice in four minutes during the second half. His goals in the 66th and 70th minutes ended any realistic possibility of a Hamburg comeback after Marco Friedl had opened the scoring.

While Niclas Füllkrug completed the victory with his 10th Bundesliga goal of the season, Njinmah was the standout performer.

His pace, directness and finishing provide Daniel Thioune with another dangerous attacking option alongside Füllkrug. His return to fitness could prove particularly vital as Bremen look to maintain their impressive start to the campaign.

Afonso Moreira delivered an impressive performance as Bayer Leverkusen defeated newly promoted Paderborn 4-0 at the BayArena.

Sources indicate that the Portuguese winger opened the scoring in the 14th minute before doubling Leverkusen’s advantage shortly after half-time. Patrik Schick and Ezequiel Fernández subsequently completed the scoring.

Moreira’s brace demonstrated his attacking potential and ability to make decisive contributions in the final third.

Industry observers note that for Leverkusen, having additional goalscoring threats alongside Schick could prove essential in their pursuit of Champions League qualification. Moreira’s performance was an encouraging indication that he can provide precisely that.

Brajan Gruda continued his impressive development as RB Leipzig secured a commanding 5-1 victory over Union Berlin.

With Leipzig leading 2-1, Gruda scored in the 72nd minute to give Martín Demichelis’ side some breathing room. Rocco Reitz and Ridle Baku subsequently added further goals to complete an outstanding second-half performance.

Following his impressive display against Augsburg before the international break, Gruda is becoming an increasingly influential figure in Leipzig’s attack.

According to recent reports, his technical ability, creativity and willingness to take on defenders give Leipzig an important attacking alternative. Demichelis’ praise following the match further underlined the growing importance of the young German international.

Michael Gregoritsch was instrumental in Augsburg’s much-needed 3-1 victory over Mainz, ending a seven-match Bundesliga winless run.

The Austrian international opened the scoring in the 19th minute before completing his brace shortly after half-time. Juma Bah also scored for Augsburg, while Mainz reduced the deficit through Ransford-Yeboah Königsdörffer.

Gregoritsch’s two goals took his Bundesliga tally to seven this season, highlighting his importance to Augsburg despite their difficult start to the campaign.

For a team struggling to establish consistency, having an experienced centre-forward capable of delivering in decisive moments could prove fundamental to their survival ambitions.

Jonathan Burkardt once again demonstrated his importance to Eintracht Frankfurt by scoring the only goal in their 1-0 victory over Hoffenheim.

The German international broke the deadlock in the 25th minute, securing three valuable points for Adi Hütter’s side in a difficult encounter at Deutsche Bank Park.

Following his brace against Paderborn before the international break, Burkardt has now scored three goals across his last two Bundesliga appearances.

In a recent development, frankfurt’s inconsistent start has raised questions about their European ambitions, but Burkardt’s goalscoring form remains one of the most encouraging aspects of Hütter’s rebuilding project. His ability to decide tight matches could prove essential as Frankfurt look to climb the Bundesliga table.

Industry observers note that matchday 10 highlighted the importance of players delivering in different circumstances. Njinmah enjoyed a memorable comeback in the Nordderby, Moreira showcased his attacking potential, Gruda continued his development, Gregoritsch helped Augsburg end their winless run and Burkardt secured an crucial victory for Frankfurt. All five produced performances worthy of recognition following the international break.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Il tecnico ha parlato con diversi giocatori; intanto il Brentford corteggia Isaksen e resta il rischio di un mercato bloccato.

Recent findings suggest that isaksen, Noslin e Taylor vogliono restare alla Lazio nonostante le attenzioni del mercato. Secondo quanto riportato da Corriere dello Sport, Gattuso ha parlato nelle ultime settimane con diversi giocatori per conoscerne gli umori e, finora, ha raccolto soltanto segnali favorevoli alla permanenza. Il tecnico spera che la sessione di gennaio non rompa il legame costruito con la squadra.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

According to recent reports, gattuso ha descritto così il rapporto nato nel gruppo: «Mi prendo un merito, aver fatto diventare questa squadra una famiglia». Nel parlare di famiglia ha richiamato anche il «senso di appartenenza» dei giocatori. È su questo legame che punta per trattenere i protagonisti della squadra, mentre cominciano a circolare le prime voci di mercato.

Il timore è quello di un nuovo ridimensionamento dopo le partenze iniziate un anno fa con Guendouzi e Castellanos e proseguite con altri giocatori, giustificate con la formula «hanno chiesto di andare via». Gattuso ha cercato di coinvolgere tutti, dando spazio anche a chi in precedenza si sentiva fuori posto. Il gruppo viene descritto attraverso i sorrisi, le parole e il clima tra i calciatori, ora al primo posto. Ai giocatori è attribuita una presa di posizione collettiva: «Siamo con Rino. Lottiamo per lui».

According to recent reports, nel rapporto con la squadra pesano anche la fame maturata dopo Zenica e l’idea di calcio affinata dal tecnico negli anni. Il modello della Lazio come gruppo familiare viene richiamato attraverso la storia del club, a partire dal primo scudetto. Sabato, all’Olimpico, i tifosi hanno cantato il nome di Gattuso.

Recent findings suggest that da giorni circolano interessamenti per gli olandesi Taylor e Noslin e per i danesi Isaksen e Provstgaard. Isaksen è stato tra i primi a esprimersi pubblicamente sul proprio futuro. Il Brentford di Matthew Benham lo corteggia: l’imprenditore britannico è noto per il lavoro svolto con Brentford e Midtjylland, il club nel quale l’esterno danese è emerso. Benham conosce bene il calcio danese.

Industry observers note that alla prospettiva della Premier League, Isaksen ha risposto: «La Premier? Voglio la Champions con la Lazio». Anche Provstgaard piace da tempo in Inghilterra. Taylor e Noslin possono attirare offerte, mentre Frattesi ha rifiutato alcune opzioni sia a gennaio sia a luglio.

Finora nessuno dei giocatori ha manifestato a Gattuso la volontà di partire. Da Taylor a Noslin, da Isaksen a Frattesi, prevale l’intenzione di proseguire il percorso con la Lazio. Le posizioni espresse dai calciatori chiamano la società a rispettare il patto costruito tra allenatore e squadra.

  • Maximilian Beier secured Borussia Dortmund a valuable point against unbeaten Arsenal in Tuesday night’s UEFA Champions League clash in London.
  • The Bundesliga leaders had to withstand early pressure, but Viktor Gyökeres left Gregor Kobel with no chance with a superb strike after ten minutes.
  • Dortmund continuously looked to exploit Arsenal’s high defensive line, but it was the Gunners who had the next golden opportunity through Declan Rice, only to be thwarted by the excellent Schlotterbeck who executed a timely block on the Englishman, who was through on goal.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Maximilian Beier secured Borussia Dortmund a valuable point against unbeaten Arsenal in Tuesday night’s UEFA Champions League clash in London.

The Bundesliga leaders had to withstand early pressure, but Viktor Gyökeres left Gregor Kobel with no chance with a superb strike after ten minutes. The Swede gathered the ball just outside the Dortmund penalty area, before striking it over Kobel and into the top corner. Dortmund’s custodian and Daniel Svensson then thwarted chances as the onslaught continued. “We had an extremely weak first 15 minutes, where we were very hesitant,” Nico Schlotterbeck told Amazon Prime.

Dortmund continuously looked to exploit Arsenal’s high defensive line, but it was the Gunners who had the next golden opportunity through Declan Rice, only to be thwarted by the excellent Schlotterbeck who executed a timely block on the Englishman, who was through on goal.

Industry observers note that arsenal took a slender 1-0 lead into the break, but Dortmund equalised ten minutes after the restart. Joane Gadou won the ball back in his own half before going on a superb run into the attacking third, before playing in Beier who cut back onto his left foot and slotted the ball under Kepa, who was deputising for the injured David Raya.

That goal clearly gave Dortmund confidence, as Jobe Bellingham saw his strike ruled out for offside after following up Julian Ryerson’s parried effort. Bellingham and Beier’s departure, though, seemed to take the sting out of Dortmund’s game, as Arsenal were on top in the final 20 minutes.

First, Gyökeres missed a sitter in the 76th minute after placing his free header wide of Kobel’s post, before a goalmouth scramble ensued four minutes later. Rice then hit the post just two minutes later, but Dortmund withstood the storm to secure a share of the spoils on a bitterly cold night.

Borussia Dortmund: Kobel (7) – Gadou (7) , Anton (6), Schlotterbeck (7) – Ryerson (5), Veerman (6), Nmecha (6), Svensson (4), Bellingham (6), Beier (7) – Silva (4).

Others: Guirassy (5), Karetsas (4), Sabitzer (5), Mane (-).

GGFN | Daniel Pinder – reporting from the Emirates Stadium.

Antonio Conte has claimed clubs are 'frightened of winning' if they have concerns over his methods after the Italian was overlooked for the Manchester United job.

Conte had been heavily linked with the role at Old Trafford, joining Julian Nagelsmann, Eddie Howe and Unai Emery among the list bookmakers' favourites to replace Michael Carrick.

Man United ultimately went with another former Chelsea and Tottenham boss in Mauricio Pochettino, paying around £10million in compensation to lure him away from being head coach of the United States' national team.

Conte, who remains out of work after leaving Napoli in the summer, has now hit back at reports suggesting Man United may have been put off by his intensity and demands.

'First, let me address the question of my method,' Conte told the Cronache di Spogliatoio podcast.

'If anyone is frightened by my method, then they are frightened of winning, because that methodology leads to victory. That is my answer.

Antonio Conte has claimed clubs are 'frightened of winning' if they have concerns over his methods after the Italian was overlooked for the Manchester United job.

Man United opted to appoint Mauricio Pochettino as head coach after sacking Michael Carrick.

Conte hit back at suggestions Man United's hierachy might have been relucant to appoint him because of his methods.

'Manchester United has such a significant history that I find it strange to imagine anyone could be afraid of an approach aimed at restoring the club to its true stature.

'(United) last won the league in 2013, under Ferguson. I have immense respect for Sir Alex Ferguson.

According to recent reports, 'I've read his book, and when I was in London, I was fortunate enough to visit his home and spend a day with him. He has an incredible passion for talking about football, though, at times, his Scottish accent can be quite hard to follow.

'Through his own methodology and approach, he made Manchester United great.

'That is why I find certain remarks almost offensive toward United; it's as if someone were placing a veto on the club's return to its own history.

According to recent reports, 'A method is what's needed to achieve major results. And if you're suggesting that this method requires hard work, well, yes, it does. Everyone has to work hard, not just the players.'.

Conte has long been known for his combustible personality - as well as an impressive winning record as a coach.

Recent findings suggest that at Chelsea, he fell out with star striker Diego Costa, centre back David Luiz and the club's board. At Napoli, he left a year after winning the Serie A title and stated there was 'too much poison, too much malice' at the club.

Conte has developed a reputation for his high intensity and demands, while the Italian famously left Tottenham after an explosive press conference attacking the club's culture.

Conte has won five Serie A titles across three clubs and won the Premier League with Chelsea.

Conte famously left Tottenham after an explosive press conference in 2023, where he labelled his players as 'selfish' and took aim at the club's culture.

The Italian, however, has overseen five Serie A title wins during his spells at Juventus, Inter Milan and Napoli, along with winning the Premier League and FA Cup with Chelsea.

It is not the first time Conte has spoken out in recent weeks following links to Old Trafford, with the 57-year-old having denied he had set 'specific conditions' about taking over at United.

La Repubblica claimed Conte wanted 'carte blanche on the transfer market' and to act as a manager, rather than a head coach, with a technical staff behind the scenes chosen by him involving 'trusted collaborators'.

'My name has been linked with numerous clubs, but there are right now no negotiations at an advanced stage,' Conte responded on social media last month.

'Following a wonderful and successful spell in charge of Napoli, I will take the time I need to consider how and when to return to management. It will be a carefully considered decision, one I will make when I believe the conditions are right.

Recent findings suggest that 'I have read reports of financial demands and requests for full control that I have supposedly already made to the clubs mentioned, as well as reservations about what has been described as my "strong personality". These reports are unfounded, as there is currently no concrete basis for such assessments.

'Should a concrete opportunity arise, that will be the time to hold discussions with the club concerned and jointly consider the terms of a potential agreement, with due regard for both parties' needs and the qualities and approach that define my work as a manager.'.

Pochettino, who landed the job at Old Trafford, has faced a whirlwind start having flown into Manchester following his final match in charge of the United States on Tuesday.

The Argentine took training for the first time on Thursday and will lead the Red Devils out for the first time on Sunday in a blockbuster clash with Liverpool at Anfield.

Pochettino takes over with Man United lying in the Premier League's relegation zone having won just one of their opening ten matches.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nell’anticipazione dell’intervista, Francesca Fagnani suggerisce la prima parola della sigla latina.

Francesco Totti è alle prese con gli acronimi SPQR e LGBTQIA+ in un’anticipazione della sua intervista a Belve. L’ex capitano della Roma fatica a ricordare il significato della prima sigla e risponde con alcune battute alle domande di Francesca Fagnani sulla seconda. Lo scambio è riportato da Cinemaserietv.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

According to recent reports, tra le prime domande dell’anteprima c’è quella su SPQR, l’acronimo latino che compare da secoli sullo stemma di Roma e che per anni è stato presente anche sulle maglie giallorosse. Totti non sembra ricordarne con precisione il significato: «SPQR erano quelle… che era… ‘na cosa che nun me ricordo bene».

Fagnani gli suggerisce la prima parola, Senatus. L’ex numero dieci prova a proseguire, poi si ferma: «Senatus? Mo’ pure il latino vuoi… Senatus Popolusco e Romanus so’ troppe frasi».

Recent findings suggest that la conduttrice passa quindi a LGBTQIA+. Totti sembra non riconoscere l’acronimo e, inizialmente, lo associa alla tecnologia: «LGBT? Nun so’ tecnologico io. LGBTQ Plus. Ma che è, un telefonino?».

Fagnani insiste con la domanda e l’ex calciatore continua sullo stesso tono ironico: «18 Plus? Ma ndo’ le tiri fuori ‘ste domande?. Ma come famo?». Il botta e risposta fa parte delle anticipazioni dell’intervista che Totti concederà alla conduttrice.

With three 1-0 wins in the Bundesliga, his BVB team faced arguably their biggest challenge of the season on Tuesday night when they faced off against Premier League champions and last season’s UEFA Champions League finalists: Arsenal.

Although going behind to a superb Viktor Gyökeres wondergoal in the tenth minute, Maximilian Beier equalised for the Bundesliga leaders ten minutes into the second period, before Jobe Bellingham saw his strike ruled out for an offside. Evidently happy with a 1-1 draw in London, Kovač praised his team’s performance.

In a recent development, “It’s a massive point for us,” Dortmund’s head coach send in his post-match press conference, attended by Get German Football News. “A big moment for all of us, for the team and for the fans who turned out in such large numbers today.

“In the end, we’re happy to take the point.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

RB Leipzig climbed into the UEFA Champions League play-off spots with a 3-1 win over French outfit Lens, thanks largely to a superb performance from the in-form Antonio Nusa, who was twice on target as the Bundesliga outfit dominated.

On paper, the hosts had what can only be described as a huge chance to get their hands on a big three points, facing a team that took the heaviest of beatings when the league phase was last in action – having shipped nine against Como, and they didn’t waste the opportunity.

Leipzig boss Martín Demichelis made three changes from the win over Union Berlin at the weekend, bringing in Maxime Esteve for Castello Lukeba at the back, Rocco Reitz for Ezechiel Banzuzi in midfield and Tidiam Gomis for Romulo up top.

Industry observers note that beginning the game on the front foot, Leipzig immediately pushed the French visitors deep into their own half. Antonio Nusa jinked his way into a couple of early shooting positions, before misfiring, but it didn’t take long for the first goal to arrive. After five minutes, Tidiam Gomis earned a free kick on the very edge of the Lens area. David Raum did the rest, scoring with the help of a hefty deflection.

Just a few minutes later, the lively Nusa latched on to a loose defensive pass, before slotting home coolly, making it 2-0 before the ten-minute mark. Abdallah Sima then got free in the Leipzig box, but couldn’t get his shot off, instead losing his footing and delivering a disappointing end to one of Lens’ only promising first-half moves.

For most of the first half, it was the home team in charge, pushing forward at every opportunity, with the visitors mustering little, both in terms of defensive nous and offensive punch.

Leipzig very nearly made it three after the restart, Brajan Gruda coming close, only to be denied by Robin Risser.

The visitors then upped their efforts, forging a number of early second-half attacks through Florian Thauvin, who failed to accurately deliver several corners, before shooting from just outside the box, only to see his effort blocked by a defender.

Recent findings suggest that it wasn’t long, though, until the Lens pressure paid off, with Matthieu Udol pulling back on 58 minutes. The French midfielder latched onto a loose ball inside the box and rifled home. Four minutes later and Sima thought that he’d levelled things, only for the offside flag to cut short the celebrations of the Senegalese forward.

The Lens players were clearly galvanised by Udol’s goal, which was followed by more visiting pressure, and as the influential Thauvin started to see more and more of the ball, an equaliser seemed nowhere near as unlikely as it did earlier in the contest.

As the game entered the final 15 minutes, the hosts wrestled back some control, alleviating the pressure by retaining possession, before launching a couple of late counter attacks, one of which very nearly restored the two-goal lead, with substitute Christopher Nkunku being denied by the leaping Robin Risser.

Risser’s late efforts ended up being for nothing when Antonio Nusa sealed the three points in stoppage time, tapping home from an Nkunku pull back, capping off what was a Man of the Match performance, pushing Leipzig into the play-off places.

RB Leipzig: Vandevoordt (6) – Raum (7), Esteve (6), Orban (6), Baku (6) – El Aynaoui (6), Reitz (7) – Nusa (9), Baumgartner (7), Gruda (7) – Gomis (7).

Others: Romulo (6), Banzuzi (6), Nkunku (7), Seiwald (6), Maksimovic (-).

Lens: Risser (6) – Todibo (5), Baidoo (5), Ganiou (5) – Udol (7), Haidara (5), Titraoui (6), Abdulhamid (5) – Thauvin (7), Sotoca (5) – Sima (5).

Others: Kadile (5), Mesloub (5), Skoras (5), Bulatovic (-).

Sources indicate that the Norwegian forward is in red-hot form right now, and that shone through the moment the game kicked off. His pace and direct approach caused countless problems for the Lens defence, who failed to handle a player, who can just as easily beat a man on the outside and cross or cut in and shoot.

Nusa’s second required little effort, but showed that he has the off-ball movement to score poacher-type goals.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

At the final whistle, the first song the stadium DJ played was Spirit of the Blues and how those relieved Evertonians lapped it up after a week of angst.

Sources indicate that their team had been on the precipice of a defeat that would have exacerbated all the frustrations that bubbled away following the chaotic conclusion to the transfer window. Indeed, it was 10 seconds over the allotted five minutes of added time when the ball fell to Ainsley Maitland-Niles.

It had been three years since the former Arsenal full-back had played in the Premier League – his last goal in England was on October 30, 2019, in an EFL Cup tie with Liverpool at Anfield that ended 5-5 – and he would not have joined Everton if their attempt to sign Kenny Tete from Fulham had not failed.

But here he was 30 yards from goal, with no need to break his stride as Manchester United’s backtracking defenders presented him with an invitation to shoot. So that’s what he did. With one perfectly timed swish of his right foot, an unlikely hero transformed the mood of a club.

Sources indicate that "That is something SPECIAL!"Ainsley Maitland-Niles earns a draw for Everton on his debut with an unbelievable 96th minute strike! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/HNdx9PxrUP.

Sources indicate that “Brilliant technique,” stated David Moyes, Everton’s manager, who had only introduced Maitland-Niles in the 77th minute after James Garner had succumbed to cramp and could run no more. “We are still getting to know Ainsley but that was a brilliant goal.”.

It has been revealed that only those with the coldest hearts would begrudge Everton this point, which was especially hard-earned given they had conceded an 88th-minute header to Benjamin Sesko. But there is no chance a disbelieving Michael Carrick will feel that way.

Benajmin Sesko puts Manchester United back in front! 👊 pic.twitter.com/MF3A9LyaY8.

According to recent reports, united should, really, have won this game comfortably. Everton were there to be exploited and when Bryan Mbuemo put them ahead early in the second half, they should have powered away into the distance. Everton’s effort was good but they were in danger of losing hope.

According to recent reports, yet, incredibly, United gave Everton two helping hands. They had not been in a position to assist last Tuesday evening, when phone calls from Merseyside to Old Trafford to take Joshua Zirkzee on loan were met with rejection. But the second half display more than made up for that.

“We’re bitterly disappointed,” said Carrick, who was one step removed from having steam puffing from his ears. “All the work that went into putting us in that position at different stages to then come away like that… it’s not a great feeling. It feels like a defeat. It’s a bit of a cliché to say.”.

But clichés are true. First United were passive when Tyrique George crashed in a brilliant right-footed drive in the 83rd minute and then, after Sesko profited from Jordan Pickford’s weak hands, they were passive again in allowing Everton to build the move that ended up with Maitland-Niles’ howitzer.

How had it come to this? It was beautiful bedlam, the kind of joy that only football delivers, but for long periods it felt like it was an opportunity for United. There was anticipation that Everton’s fans would create a furnace but there was also the fear it would be dispiritingly quiet.

Had this fixture been at Goodison Park, with its steep stands, tight confines and acoustics that split your ears, United would have been aware of the siege mentality as soon as their bus rolled up outside the stadium but their new sparkling home is rather more hospitable.

Sources indicate that this is no criticism of the home crowd – it is anything but. Why should it always fall to them to bail out the failings of those in charge when those in charge, specifically the executives and recruitment department, have given them scant reason to have hope?

The route to victory for United, then, was relatively straightforward: for all Everton’s initial huff and puff, it always appeared that it would be a case of the away team repeating the simple things, retaining their concentration and waiting for a breakthrough.

It could have come as early as the eighth minute. Luke Shaw’s deep cross to the back post picked out Mbuemo, whose cushioned header invited Bruno Fernandes to take aim but the Portuguese’s volley clipped the crossbar with Pickford stranded.

Industry observers note that united dominated and Marcus Rashford was central to it all, a scampering presence down the left who gave Merlin Röhl, playing as an auxiliary right-back, all kinds of problems. The only thing missing from his opening 45 minutes was a goal.

It has been revealed that when Mbuemo scored so early after the break, it felt as if this was going to be one puncture too many for Everton to withstand and the anticipation was United would get the job done. In all fairness to Moyes, however, he was not in the mood to accept excuses.

His substitutions were all positive, with Jack Grealish changing the mood and Hayden Hackney providing dynamism. But it was the former Middlesbrough man who drove forward to give George, whose loan move from Chelsea was made permanent in June, the opportunity to smash an 83rd-minute bullet past Senne Lammens.

"That was unanswerable!"What a way for Tyrique George to open his account for Everton! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/c0HPRjWUia.

Recent findings suggest that “I told the players there would be no excuses and the players all agreed,” Moyes said. “They have hugely bought into it. And, you know, sometimes when you have [fewer] players it means everybody has to be ready. Sometimes when you have a small squad you have to find a way of making it work.”.

Sources indicate that they did just that. Pickford should have saved the header from Sesko that looked as though it had given United the lift, but Everton, with their manager belligerent and their fans sensing all was not lost, had other ideas. The noise they generated as Maitland-Niles’s goal went in was unique to this stadium.

As Moyes celebrated, shaking his fists and revelling in the positive turn of events, Carrick put his hand across his face and shook his head repeatedly. All the while, Everton’s fans sang I guess that’s why they call it the Blues. United’s head coach certainly had them. Everton, simply, had relief.

2 - For just the second time in the last 50 years, Manchester United have conceded 2+ goals in each of their first three games of a league season, along with 2020-21.Leaky. pic.twitter.com/B2Dk6Ioxkq.

According to recent reports, it felt like a win. The crowd was with us, we fight to the end and that’s how you get that type of result.

It’s amazing. Everyone wants to start like that and fortunately I did. I put my foot through it and it ended up in the top corner which I’m happy about.

According to recent reports, I came here to work hard. It’s a team full of hard workers and I fit right in. I’m going to show I can pull my weight and give as much as everyone else, if not a little bit more.

Even I have a lump in my throat to see him do that after his original move to Everton in August 2021 was stymied by a late change of heart by Mikel Arteta. Don’t normally approve of badge kissers but he has waited such a long time for that and must have thought his chance had gone.

Recent findings suggest that just time to kick off before the whistle goes. Probably a fair result and that goal from Maitland-Niles was good enough to win a game never mind save it.

Everton 2 Manchester United 2 (Maitland-Niles) Stunning strike! Mazraoui had tackled Dewsbury-Hall in the box after more good work between Grealish and Hackney down the left. But the tackle diverted the ball to Maitland-Niles 25 yards out. And he wrapped his instep around a shot on debut that bent into the top left corner. What a goal!

"That is something SPECIAL!"Ainsley Maitland-Niles earns a draw for Everton on his debut with an unbelievable 96th minute strike! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/HNdx9PxrUP.

It has been revealed that grealish’s beguiling feet dazzle Mazraoui down the Everton left as he tricks him to reach the byline. He cuts back a pass to Barry who tees up Hackney for a shot that he wafts miles over the bar. Grealish gives him a look as if to say, “Really?”.

It has been revealed that george finds himself in a near identical spot from which he scored and tries again with a thumping shot that flies into the side-netting via Lammens’ finger tips. He was offside on this occasion, though.

Five minutes of added time for Everton to level again.

According to recent reports, everton 1 Manchester United 2 (Sesko) Sesko wins the ball in the middle and works it out to Bruno Fernandes running down the left. He stops, faces up Maitland-Niles and waits for Shaw to gallop past him before rolling it into the left-back’s stride. Shaw fizzes over a cross that parts Tarkowski’s luxuriant barnet and Sesko, lurking on his shoulder, buries it from eight yards.

Benajmin Sesko puts Manchester United back in front! 👊 pic.twitter.com/MF3A9LyaY8.

Recent findings suggest that as Dominic notes, below, Manchester United have been asking for this. They have been toothless since Mbeumo’s goal and the only significant threat, Rashford, was taken off for a left-back.

Everton 1 Man Utd 1 (George) A rasping, rising shot that beats Lammens at his near post. He absolutely larruped it after good work by Hackney to put him in space down the right of the box.

Recent findings suggest that good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of Everton vs Manchester United from Hill Dickinson Stadium. The hosts have made a creditable start on the field but four points from their opening two games cannot gloss over the discontent fostered by the owners and executives because of the credibility gap between their talk about recruitment and their paltry achievements.

The fact that their comeback against Bournemouth to earn a draw last week was achieved with Beto, Tim Iroegbunum and Iliman Ndiaye on the field and all three have now been sold with only Jack Grealish returning on loan to compensate tells its own story.

According to recent reports, speak to supporters and it is emblematic of ownership, they fear, who are prioritising Roma and view the Hill Dickinson as a terrific multisport and concert venue with a heritage football club attached. The bullishness of Angus Kinnear, the chief executive, rings hollower with each pronouncement and it is little wonder that the fans are so disenchanted.

David Moyes will not walk away but once again he has been sent into the fray against teams with £250m midfields armed with a spud gun. Having noted that, we should not underestimate his capacity to rally the old “dogs of war” spirit even if the crowd is still yearning more for a “school of science” revival.

Manchester United won on their first visit to the Hill Dickinson last season when Benjamin Sesko came off the bench to score the only goal of the game and give Michael Carrick a fifth win in six league games as caretaker manager. They were far more fluid in their forward play during the victory over Ipswich last week but it was against an error-stricken defence and they continued to be as worryingly open at the back as they had been against Hull City in the opening round of fixtures with Luke Shaw and Lisandro Martínez having brain fades.

Shaw is a doubt today, along with Mason Mount, while Amad Diallo, Matthijs de Ligt, Carlos Baleba and Manuel Ugarte have all been ruled out. Only Christian Norgaard is absent for Everton but so thin is their squad, they will cast covetous glances at Man Utd’s bench, not least at Joshua Zirkzee who was the subject of a very late rejected bid on deadline day.

The Preview: It's time for Hibs boss Reedijk to bring sunshine back to Leith

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 16:03 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 16:18 EST, 20 November 2026.

Hibernian supporters know all too well the dangers associated with getting one’s hopes up.

It’s a road they’ve been down time and time again, only to end up with that same familiar sickening feeling in the pit of their stomach at the end of it.

Which is why any talk of the Edinburgh club experiencing some sort of mini-revival should quite rightly be taken with more than a large pinch of salt.

Let’s not forget, at the start of the month, latest boss Marink Reedijk had picked up a paltry point from his four games in charge since taking the reins from David Gray.

Performances weren’t up to much either.

A statement win over Hearts at Hampden to book their Premier Sports Cup final spot was backed up with an emphatic 4-0 dismantling of Aberdeen up at Pittodrie.

Hibs manager Marink Reedijk is still searching for his first victory at Easter Road.

Industry observers note that credit where it’s due, of course. Both victories were hard-earned and thoroughly deserved.

In a recent development, but it’s important not to read too much in to either of them. Players going above and beyond in a derby clash should be a given, while the Dons appeared to have chucked it altogether under the stewardship of former manager Stephen Robinson long before Hibs turned up in the Granite City.

The real test begins this weekend with the visit of Dundee United, as Reedijk’s men look to secure a first home Premiership win in over seven months.

The fans have been crying out for entertainment in Leith for far longer than that. In the latter days of Gray’s reign, the atmosphere at Easter Road was verging on toxic.

Reedijk needs to change that, and now has two games against the Dundee clubs over the next four days to get the momentum swinging in the opposite direction.

Continuing to get the best out of his midfield three will be key to that.

In a recent development, the reintroduction of Joe Newell to the starting XI has paid off significant-time. Not so much in terms of the stats, but rather what he allows Miguel Chaiwa and Josh Mulligan to do.

The former was linked with a move to Celtic over the summer, but looked miles off it in the early weeks of the campaign until Newell lined up alongside him.

Chaiwa can be guilty of trying to carry out too many jobs in the middle of the park, but Newell’s calming influence has enabled him to stick to what he’s good at — namely breaking up the play and moving the ball on to his more creative team-mates in front of him.

There’s no doubt the Zambian is at his best when he keeps things simple.

Joe Newell has provided a calming influence in the middle of the park amid this upturn in form.

Newell’s presence has also freed Mulligan to play further up the field rather than on the fringes of his own box, where he was popping up far too often a couple of months ago. He’s wasted back there.

If he can add some more goals and assists to his name over the next few, there is every chance he can play himself in to the thoughts of Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli ahead of the next set of internationals.

It should be an intriguing battle this afternoon in the engine room, with United boasting the most cohesive midfield group in the top flight with Dylan Tait, Lyall Cameron and Zidane Iqbal.

Of course, even if Hibs deliver in that sense, it may count for very little if the guys at the top end of the pitch can’t do the business. The lack of cutting edge has been an ongoing concern. Four goals against Aberdeen doesn't change that.

Owen Elding appears to be Reedijk’s preferred option in the central striker role, but while the young Irishman has shown flashes of his potential, he has offered little to suggest he can be relied upon to find the net on a consistent basis.

The problem is, can anyone? Record-signing Thibault Klidje may have opened his league account for the season against the Dons, however we’ve seen enough to know that he isn’t the answer.

Ante Suto is in the same boat, while Stoke City loanee Nathan Lowe has struggled for both game time and form.

Industry observers note that and as for Rabbi Matondo? Well, the wait goes on to see any real return on that investment. Early days, mind you.

That Martin Boyle remains Hibs’ main goalscoring threat is troubling, especially given that the veteran can’t even be considered a nailed-on starter these days.

It has been revealed that there are a significant number of players — across all areas of the park — fighting for their future at the club. Indeed, you would imagine Reedijk is counting down the days until January when he will look to freshen up the squad with guys more suited to his style.

Lyall Cameron has been a key man behind Dundee United's surge up the Premiership table.

Hibs should use today’s opponents as an example of how patience can pay off.

Industry observers note that it’s fair to say that Jim Goodwin has never been Mr. Popular in and around Tannadice. Goodness knows why.

Many fans were calling for his head as recently as the summer after failing to secure a top-six finish last term, but he is slowly but surely starting to win over his doubters.

Make no mistake, this season presents a golden opportunity for United to seriously challenge for third spot.

You never know what you’re going to get from Hearts on any given week, while this is very much uncharted territory for Falkirk.

And let’s face it, nobody would expect the likes of Hibs, Aberdeen or Motherwell to claw themselves into contention.

While everyone else tries to stumble their way through a period of transition, United’s consistency – both on and off the park – could prove to be the difference.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Dopo le rassicurazioni a Gattuso, il club valuta un ritocco dell’ingaggio: prima affronterà i contratti in scadenza nel 2028.

It has been revealed that kenneth Taylor vuole restare alla Lazio a gennaio e il club pensa a un ritocco del suo ingaggio. Secondo quanto riportato da Il Messaggero, il centrocampista ha rassicurato Gattuso dopo l’interesse arrivato dalla Premier League e dalla Juventus. La società intende occuparsi prima dei contratti in scadenza nel 2028, poi affrontare anche la sua situazione.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

According to recent reports, durante la sosta della scorsa settimana a Formello, Rino era in allarme per le sirene del mercato. Sono bastate poche parole di Taylor per tranquillizzarlo. Il giocatore gli ha confermato l’interesse ricevuto: «È tutto vero, i miei agenti mi hanno informato.» Gli ha però chiarito che non intende partire a gennaio: «Ma ho già detto che a gennaio non ci penso proprio ad andare via.».

Recent findings suggest that taylor ha espresso a Gattuso anche il suo obiettivo: «Voglio restare qui e aiutare la Lazio a tornare in Champions». Il tecnico non si aspettava questa risposta e ne è stato molto felice. Isaksen e Provstgaard gli avevano già promesso fedeltà e appartenenza. A 24 anni, Taylor è descritto come un giocatore già affermato, pronto per un salto di livello e capace di trovare posto in molte grandi squadre italiane e non solo.

Anche Fabiani e Lotito vogliono trattenere Taylor. Se il suo percorso proseguirà così, a giugno potrebbero non bastare neppure 40 milioni di euro per convincerli a trattare con Juventus, Brentford e Bournemouth. La Lazio vuole ricompensarlo per l’attaccamento mostrato e per aver rinunciato a guadagni più alti offerti altrove.

Dopo aver affrontato i contratti in scadenza nel 2028, il club parlerà di un possibile adeguamento per Kenneth, che percepisce 1,7 milioni di euro fino al 2030. A febbraio riceverà il secondo premio fedeltà da 190mila euro, dopo aver scelto per la seconda volta di restare in biancoceleste. Acquistato dall’Ajax per meno di 17 milioni di euro, con il club olandese che conserva il 10% su una futura rivendita, Taylor si è rivelato un colpo straordinario per la Lazio.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sebastian Hoeness, allenatore dello Stoccarda, ha parlato in conferenza stampa alla vigilia dell'impegno di Champions League contro l'Inter. Qui le sue considerazioni: "Stiller? So che vorreste la formazione, lui ha recuperato ed è in grado di giocare, vale per tutti gli altri. Contro lo Schalke i ragazzi hanno fatto ciò che gli ho chiesto, soprattutto in alcune fasi della partita. Ci è mancato l'ultimo passaggio, non abbiamo fatto ottime scelte, ma abbiamo comunque creato diverse occasioni. Dobbiamo capire che se avessimo per caso segnato un gol l'impressione dei media sarebbe stata diversa. Veniamo da uno 0-0 e di sicuro vorremmo vincere di più e non perdere ancora tanti punti per strada. Abbiamo anche da pensare alla Champions League, ma avremmo dovuto avere almeno due punti in più in Europa se pensiamo a quanto fatto in casa dell'Atletico. La sfortuna ci ha accompagnato nel percorso, speriamo di riuscire a fare meglio domani".

Sources indicate that undav non ha brillato contro lo Schalke. "Non è solamente lui il tema, sono tutti sempre in discussione. Che lui polarizzi lo sappiamo, ma non voglio parlare di un singolo. Non abbiamo segnato contro lo Schalke, ma è una responsabilità che riguarda tutti".

In a recent development, che impressione ti fa questo stadio?"Siamo contentissimi di essere qui, abbiamo fatto un giro nello stadio ed è stato impressionante. E' alto, enorme, come lo ricordavo quando l'ho visto da spettatore da adolescente. Guardo tante partite in tv, ho visto anche il derby. Questo stadio ha una storia pazzesca, incluso il capitolo dei mondiali del '90. Siamo felici di poter giocare qui ed essere parte della storia di questo stadio. E' fantastico anche senza tifosi, non vediamo l'ora di goderci l'atmosfera domani sera".

Che ricordi hai della prima partita vista qui?"Sì, di fatto ho visto qui la prima partita in cui ho preso consapevolezza del calcio. Abbiamo visto la partita della Germania qui nel '90 e da allora la passione è cresciuta dentro di me".

Industry observers note that ti aspettavi di venire qui ad affrontare l'Inter con un punto in più in classifica?"Devo essere molto sincero, era impossibile aspettarselo. siamo davanti e faremo di tutto perché l'Inter rimanga dietro. Ci vogliamo misurare contro loro, sono tra le più grandi squadre in Europa. Noi siamo in grado di tenere testa anche ad avversarie così forti".

Recent findings suggest that ha visto Atalanta-Inter?"Ho visto Atalanta-Inter live, ma anche altre partite in differita. L'Inter è organizzata benissimo, ha un grandissimo allenatore e grandi individualità. Riesce a trovare una commistione tra la grande organizzazione, con schemi molto chiari, e il valore dei singoli. Vedendola da lontano la vedo come un unico collettivo che funziona molto bene, ha tutte le corde accordate quando i singoli si muovono d'insieme".

Industry observers note that si parla delle amnesie difensive dell'Inter in Italia."Abbiamo visto che per l'Inter è insolito prendere così tanti gol, non so se ci siano falle strutturali. Non penso che l'Inter giocherà con la stessa difesa di Bergamo. Ci sono anche delle defezioni, ma hanno una squadra fantastica e noi dobbiamo mostrare di cosa siamo capaci, sfruttando magari i loro punti deboli. Vogliamo portare la nostra proposta di calcio, si tratterà di cogliere momenti che saranno magari più favorevoli per noi e sfruttarli al meglio".

In a recent development, il momento dell'Inter può favorirvi in qualche modo?"Abbiamo visto tutti insieme la partita contro l'Atalanta, osservando i loro meccanismi e tenendo in considerazione ogni aspetto. Vediamo che cercano di giocare di sponda sulla punta, magari domani giocherà Lautaro, ma hanno anche grande tecnica da abbinare alla fisicità. Dimarco ha un piede sinistro che non devo neanche raccontarvi, per esempio. Abbiamo una grande sfida davanti a noi: tenere conto di tutte le componenti dell'Inter".

#187371. Breaking: Mauricio Pochettino must fix a club stuck in a constant cycle of failure. The latest Man United boss has the personality but the squad is a mish-mash and where he sits as a coach is a great unknown, writes IAN LADYMAN

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1336 w)

Breaking: Mauricio Pochettino must fix a club stuck in a constant cycle of failure. The latest Man United boss has the personality but the squad is a mish-mash and where he sits as a coach is a great unknown, writes IAN LADYMAN

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1336 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 16:51 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 17:07 EST, 20 November 2026.
  • In a soft-focus Sky TV interview that followed Mauricio Pochettino’s opening press conference on Friday, the Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada revealed there had been a ‘buzz’ about the club since the arrival of their latest manager.
  • Whether he was speaking metaphorically or referring to the sound of drones stealing Pochettino’s training secrets from above only he will know.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By IAN LADYMAN, FOOTBALL EDITOR.

Published: 16:51 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 17:07 EST, 20 November 2026.

In a soft-focus Sky TV interview that followed Mauricio Pochettino’s opening press conference on Friday, the Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada revealed there had been a ‘buzz’ about the club since the arrival of their latest manager.

Whether he was speaking metaphorically or referring to the sound of drones stealing Pochettino’s training secrets from above only he will know.

As is usually the case these days, much about the modern United remains unclear.

But what we do know after welcoming the eighth full-time manager since the days of Sir Alex Ferguson is that once again England’s biggest football club is relying on a personality lift to drag them back to their feet.

Sources indicate that this is what happens when you get things wrong for so long, when you buy the wrong players and install executives who appear to be learning on the job. You end up hiring and firing managers, waiting for the one who finally arrives with the magic dust, the capacity to somehow create something greater than the sum of the rather wonky parts.

Listening to Pochettino here – a talented coach and a good person – was to occasionally think back to words spoken in the weeks of their arrivals on this territory by predecessors such as Ruben Amorim and Erik ten Hag.

For they too were asked about such intangibles as culture and mood and philosophy. They too were asked about more prosaic football matters such as match fitness.

It’s a conversational cycle that tells a story of recurring and systematic football failure.

Mauricio Pochettino faced reporters in his first press conference as Manchester United boss on Friday.

A drone captured footage of Pochettino's first training session on Thursday.

Amorim – back on a grim, foggy day exactly two years ago – was asked about Marcus Rashford and whether he had been right to spend time off in Latest York days before the new United manager walked through the door.

Here, Pochettino could justifiably have been asked about another forward Bryan Mbeumo spending the wee hours of Thursday morning playing the newly released Grand Theft Auto video game when he probably should have been asleep.

This is the United that Pochettino is now being asked to fix, a club where names and faces change but problems remain the same.

The Berrada interview was actually more enlightening than Pochettino’s carefully managed introduction to the wider media.

Certainly it was interesting to listen to his assertion that nine defensive players in one squad was enough. In football, as United are discovering yet again, it’s not necessarily the quantity that matters but the quality.

One point did resonate rather more deeply, though, and that was the one Berrada – once of Manchester City – made about United’s players needing a manager capable of dealing with the scrutiny of the club and who could shield some of his players from all that comes with it.

The recently-departed Michael Carrick did look rather lost on the touchline in the final tumultuous weeks of his time as manager. He didn’t look an awful lot more comfortable in front of the TV cameras either.

Bryan Mbeumo posted this picture after the midnight release of Grand Theft Auto VI.

Industry observers note that in the dressing room? Well, he lost the loyalty of his captain Bruno Fernandes towards the end and that is never a good sign.

In a recent development, pochettino will do rather better at all that. The former Chelsea, PSG and Tottenham manager has a personality and a charisma that could fill an aircraft hangar. His players will arrive at Anfield for his opening game on Sunday feeling better about themselves than they have for some time.

United have hired some confidence and some authority and some experience at a time when they desperately need it, even if Berrada’s claim that they had to call the USA Federation last week to check on his release clause suggested this is an appointment made rather on the hoof.

It is, however, the impact that Pochettino can bring over time on a jumbled squad put together for six different managers over an incredible 12 years that will define him. Here, the 54-year-old undoubtedly faces challenges.

Talking this week to someone associated with Tottenham about Pochettino’s progressive seasons there between 2014 and 2019, I was reminded of the quality that the Argentinian was given to work with.

Pochettino's Spurs side harnessed the attacking power of stars including Harry Kane and Heung-min Son.

The French international goalkeeper, Hugo Lloris, the Belgian central defensive partnership of Toby Alderweireld and Jan Vertonghen, England international defenders Kyle Walker, Danny Rose and Kieran Trippier and, further forward, the burgeoning attacking talents of Dele Alli, Christian Eriksen, Heung-min Son and Harry Kane.

In a recent development, it was a prototype Premier League football team, both in talent, age, fitness and physicality. That was why, in 2016, it almost won it.

Industry observers note that pochettino does not have this at Old Trafford. He doesn’t have anything like it. He has some talented players. The fact he inherits a team in the bottom three is down to Carrick’s inadequacies.

But this United squad is a mish-mash and it serves a purpose to ask how many would get in that old Spurs team we talk about.

Fernandes? Maybe. Mbeumo? Probably. That is about it and that, frankly, is where United are right now.

Recent findings suggest that pochettino has long wanted this job. It’s not a posting of convenience for him. Like others before him – men like Jose Mourinho and Louis van Gaal – he has long since coveted the cachet, the stature and the power of this remarkable football institution.

Mourinho and Van Gaal had better players than Pochettino is being handed and they both still failed, largely because they were shown to be coaches already over the top of that hill that both had worked so desperately hard to climb.

Mbeumo is one of the few United players who might have got into Pochettino's Spurs side.

It has been revealed that where does Pochettino sit in terms of his own personal and professional growth? That is such a hard question to answer and will be utterly fundamental to how he travels in the weeks and months to come.

Sitting here fresh from the training ground and strangely seeming to question whether the glass of water in front of him was fit to drink, Pochettino declared himself to be in his coaching prime.

‘I am a much better coach now,’ he stated.

The proof or otherwise of that will only be revealed out on the grass. For all that he can plead valid mitigation, Pochettino was not hugely impressive in Paris or at Stamford Bridge. Before he starts to talk about dysfunctional football clubs, he may wish to take a look at his new surroundings.

Liverpool away feels like something of a free hit. Sporting in Lisbon on Wednesday less so and Brentford at home next Saturday definitely not. And so it begins. A run of 12 games in six and a half weeks that may well see Pochettino crawling into January begging for fresh legs and latest players.

The new manager remarked here that he wishes to be across transfers and little wonder. When he looks at the mistakes made in that regard by a succession of United regimes and executives, he may indeed question what it is they put in the water in the north-west.

United fans will perhaps appreciate that one of the ‘higher ups’ at Old Trafford has finally put his head above the parapet, even if they question some of what Berrada said. That’s been overdue.

Recent findings suggest that in terms of their newly introduced manager, they can be forgiven for keeping a lid on any excitement. Many of them have simply been wearied by the cycle.

Belahyane viene paragonato ad Almeyda, mentre Mandas richiama Marchegiani per le qualità tra i pali e nelle uscite.

Sources indicate that la Lazio di Gattuso ha raccolto nelle prime dodici giornate più punti di quella del 2000, considerata tra le più forti della storia biancoceleste per l’organico al completo. Secondo quanto riportato da Il Messaggero, Da quando la vittoria vale tre punti, soltanto la Juventus, prima con Capello e poi con Allegri, ha fatto meglio. È da questi numeri che Il Messaggero parte per accostare le due squadre, pur tenendo distinte le rispettive epoche.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

According to recent reports, rino, Frattesi e gli altri biancocelesti continuano a guardare al traguardo dei 40 punti, indicato come quota della salvezza matematica. Dopo la vittoria sul Lecce, il tecnico calabrese aveva spiegato: «E dopo parleremo di altro, con maggiore tranquillità».

Sources indicate that il confronto con la squadra del secondo scudetto riguarda anche lo spogliatoio. Gattuso vi ha portato un clima che richiama, con le dovute proporzioni, quello creato da Eriksson ventisei anni fa. Nella Lazio di allora, però, l’armonia non era quella di oggi: convivevano il gruppo degli ex Samp, guidato da Roberto Mancini, e quello degli argentini, senza un capo designato ma rappresentato dalle personalità di Veron e Simeone.

Il paragone suggerito dalla partita contro il Lecce è quello tra Belahyane e Almeyda. Il marocchino intercetta palloni e li sottrae agli avversari commettendo raramente fallo, come faceva l’argentino. Almeyda era chiamato Capitan Uncino per il modo in cui usava il piede destro per portare via il pallone; Belahyane si affida invece alla rapidità della corsa e all’appoggio del corpo sul rivale per interrompere l’azione.

Sources indicate that tra i portieri, Mandas richiama Luca Marchegiani: entrambi efficaci tra i pali, dotati di personalità sulle palle alte e meno talentuosi nel gioco con i piedi. A Marchegiani costò il posto in Nazionale un errore che Sacchi non gli perdonò.

In a recent development, A centrocampo, Frattesi ricorda Nedved quando arriva nei pressi dell’area pronto a colpire. Il ceco era un attaccante aggiunto per Zoff ed Eriksson; Davide è l’incursore della squadra di Gattuso. Alcuni movimenti di Taylor richiamano Stankovic, più potente soprattutto nel tiro dalla distanza. L’olandese viene accostato anche a Simeone per la capacità di contribuire con gol e assist senza dare nell’occhio.

Come per il Como, quota 12 è l’obiettivo minimo, perché in mezzo ci sono i due major match contro il Borussia (Dortmund) e il Liverpool (San Siro), repliche delle sfide dell’anno scorso: ko in casa con i Reds, successo in Germania con i gialloneri. L’Inter di coppa di una volta non resterebbe a secco. L’ultima lascia qualche perplessità. Lo Stoccarda non è facile da leggere, pari con l’Atletico e a terra sul campo del Galatasaray. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By MATT BARLOW, FOOTBALL WRITER.

Published: 17:30 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 17:35 EST, 20 November 2026.

Mykhailo Mudryk is still two weeks away from a Tottenham return after a suffering setback to his recovery from an ankle injury.

Mudryk, who has played only 16 minutes since joining on loan from Chelsea, clashed with the Ukrainian FA this week when he blamed them for his positive drug test which ruled him out of football for almost two years.

He also risked the wrath of Spurs fans by admitting he only made the move across London to recover his fitness before returning to Stamford Bridge where Blues boss Xabi Alonso was 'counting on him'.

And he managed to annoy both Chelsea and Spurs fans by revealing, during the same YouTube interview, that he wanted to sign for Arsenal when he moved to the Premier League in January 2023 but his agent forced through the move with the best commission.

'I can understand the fans, but Mudryk is a good guy,' said Spurs boss De Zerbi, who worked with the Ukraine international at Shakhtar Dontetsk and convinced him to resist interest from Brentford and Coventry and be reunited in North London.

In a recent development, 'He's a good player. He suffered a lot for the situation in the last couple of years. He has just one thing to do, show on the pitch his qualities, show on the pitch that now he's playing for Tottenham. Tottenham is a big club, like the other clubs, not less at all.'.

Mykhailo Mudryk admitted he joined Tottenham to regain fitness before returning to Chelsea, while also stating he had wanted to sign for Arsenal in 2023 before his transfer to the Blues.

Roberto De Zerbi acknowledged Tottenham fans' views on Mudryk's comments, but insisted the winger has 'suffered a lot' following his doping ban.

Chelsea paid £86million for Mudryk but he made little impression before he was hit with a four-year ban in 2024, which was wiped out this summer enabling him to return to competition.

'He has no responsibility in this part,' said De Zerbi. 'Now his focus is just on the ball or just on the football. He has a substantial chance to play with us because Tottenham is a big club. He knows very well the coach, he knows very well the style of play.

Industry observers note that 'He knows I give him total confidence to show what he is. So to move the focus in the right direction, in a good direction. But I think he's working hard to recover and to play earlier.'.

Mudryk made his Spurs debut as a sub at Nottingham Forest in September but injured an ankle in training a few days later. He was initially expected to be out for two months with Saturday's game against Ipswich his target to return.

Sources indicate that 'The plan was to be available for Ipswich or Sunderland,' mentioned De Zerbi, who will serve a touchline ban against Ipswich for three yellow cards. 'Then he felt not pain but he was not comfortable last week. And they take two weeks more, and step by step we're going to see the situation.'.

James Maddison's limited involvement for Tottenham relates to a niggling hip injury dating back to pre-season.

Maddison has been an unused sub in two Spurs games since limping off when the problem flared up at Chelsea, on his second start of the season and his second start in six days.

Roberto De Zerbi confirmed ahead of Saturday's game against Ipswich that it had been the same problem which dogged Maddison through the summer as he fought back from a serious knee injury.

The Spurs boss revealed how his physical condition had suffered from not training regularly and reminded the 29-year-old England midfielder he could only make an impact in the Premier League in peak condition.

De Zerbi confirmed James Maddison is available to face Ipswich but stressed the midfielder needs to push himself to reach his peak physical condition.

'It is not a big injury, but he was not able to work,' explained De Zerbi. 'He had a problem with his hip. The same as preseason. It's not a big problem but if you don't work consistently you lose the physical condition and to play in this level of competition you have to stay in the top physical condition.'.

Maddison, who turns 30 on Monday, missed most of last season with a cruciate knee injury and has played only 195 minutes this season. His return was further complicated by a shoulder injury after coming on at Brentford on the opening game of the season.

'He is still young, 29 years is not old,' stated De Zerbi. 'He has to push and demand of himself the top in terms of physical condition, because if he is 80 or 90 per cent of his physical condition he makes the difference for us, he changes the games.'.

Maddison and Destiny Udogie have both trained fully through the international break and are available to face Ipswich.

'He worked very well from the Wednesday after Leeds,' noted De Zerbi. 'From Chelsea to the Leeds game, he worked just three times on the pitch at the training ground.

In a recent development, 'If you don't work during the week you risk injury and lose the normal physical condition you need to play Premier League. The same for Udogie. When they work and are fit to work, they have many chances to play, especially Maddison because a special player.'.

It has been revealed that maddison's first start of the season came against Coventry when he scored the opener and inspired Spurs to their first win. He barely trained but started again in the win at Chelsea five days later, where he broke down early in the second half and was replaced by Conor Gallagher.

Sources indicate that de Zerbi made it clear there were no problems connected to Maddison being pictured out at a pub in Coventry after the defeat at Leeds. It was the last game before the international break and the first of three days off.

'I am angry because next time he has to invite me,' joked the Spurs boss and he added: 'I am happy. I know when my players work well. If they are serious on the pitch, off the pitch they can do what they want. I'm not a policeman.

'James is top professional, top guy, top player. The private life is not our problem if they work well and they are serious, and give their best for the club, the shirt and the fans, and he is perfect when it comes to that.'.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Emery always springs into life on European nights and his reconstructed team secured their first win and goals of the season to leave Villa’s 1,700 fans singing in the rain.
  • Ten summer signings have arrived during a summer of upheaval, which included plenty of high-profile departures after the club’s Europa League triumph in May.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Unai Emery is building Aston Villa 2.0 and this was a night when his newly introduced kids on the block produced clear signs of lift-off for the next chapter.

Emery always springs into life on European nights and his reconstructed team secured their first win and goals of the season to leave Villa’s 1,700 fans singing in the rain.

Ten summer signings have arrived during a summer of upheaval, which included plenty of high-profile departures after the club’s Europa League triumph in May.

Yet this was an evening that will have further energised Emery on his return to the Champions League.

Nicolas Jackson, Zion Suzuki and João Gomes embody this upcoming Villa team and all stood out here in Bruges.

Record £65m signing Jackson’s fine individual goal proved to be the winner to settle a chaotic, absorbing contest with the Belgian Pro League champions.

Recent findings suggest that jackson adds a third for Aston Villa after Sommer comes rushing out of his box! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/HZ1x3BkfK0.

Suzuki, the £30m replacement for Emiliano Martínez, has clear presence in goal and he is Villa’s version of former Manchester City goalkeeper Ederson with his wide array of passing.

Gomes was also industrious in midfield to recover from what was a nightmarish debut at Brighton, where he was sent off after 40 minutes.

Despite all the changes to this team, talismanic captain John McGinn remains essential to Villa. He became their all-time leading goalscorer in major European competitions with his 12th goal and led by example again, as he has done so many times.

McGinn strikes to put Villa ahead in Bruges! 💥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FJnuxSwYwo.

There were also hints of a strong defensive partnership developing between Pau Torres and Victor Lindelof, following the sale of Ezri Konsa to Arsenal last month.

“Fantastic, fantastic,” purred Emery at one point in the second half from the technical area, and Villa’s season now appears up and running.

Sources indicate that emery stated: “This was another step forward and I am so happy and thankful for this. The old players need to keep our standards high and show everyone this is the only way we can achieve the process and reach our targets.

“It’s very important to start the Champions League with three points and hopefully this will give us confidence for the league. We are improving and we must work hard – it is the only way.”.

Although Emery has established a reputation as the Europa League king, winning that trophy five times, this competition has proved more difficult to master.

His best run was reaching the semi-finals in the 2021-22 season, when his Villarreal side lost to Liverpool.

It remains a tournament in which he is desperate to make an impression, with Villa returning to Champions League duty here for the first time since their thrilling encounter with Paris St-Germain in April 2025.

Only five of that starting XI from the second leg of the quarter-final remain and one of them, midfielder Amadou Onana, is out until next year after sustaining a serious knee injury at the World Cup with Belgium.

With European heavyweights Barcelona, PSG and Borussia Dortmund to come in the league phase, this always felt like a game Villa probably needed to win.

They had only managed one shot on target so far this season before arriving in this historic city, but scored three goals before half-time.

In a recent development, their opener came against the run of play in the 11th minute, with McGinn casually finding the corner after a lung-bursting run from Torres. McGinn has overtaken former Villa striker Ollie Watkins at the top of the club’s continental goalscoring charts.

Brugge briefly wobbled but were level eight minutes later when Hugo Vetlesen swept home from 10 yards, capitalising on space in the penalty box.

Sources indicate that vetlesen draws Club Brugge level against Aston Villa! ⚡📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/4ZYwPcMHim.

In a recent development, villa were back in front less than 160 seconds later, with Gomes teeing up Emiliano Buendía for an easy finish. Gomes was released in the box by a clever backheel from Jackson.

Recent findings suggest that buendia restores Villa's lead just minutes after Club Brugge's equaliser, and Unai Emery is LOVING it! 🙌📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/h2WGkwkTI1.

Two minutes before half-time Yann Sommer, Club Brugge’s new goalkeeper, then had a severe rush of blood to the head by racing from his goal to almost the halfway line in an attempt to intercept Torres’s long pass.

According to recent reports, jackson edged the ball past him and held off a defender to calmly slot into the empty net. He underlined in many moments why Emery has pursued him for so long, after the pair established a strong rapport at Villarreal.

Villa appeared relatively comfortable in the second half until Aaron Wan-Bissaka was judged to have handled a cross from Joaquin Seys, after referee Sandro Schärer was advised by VAR to review the incident on his TV monitor.

It was a simple decision and Nicolò Tresoldi put away the penalty to stir life back into the home supporters.

Recent findings suggest that club Brugge are back in it from the penalty spot after Wan-Bissaka's handball! 👀📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pEanRJvimu.

Sources indicate that villa defended resolutely as time began to tick away with Suzuki providing authority in goal. The first Japanese goalkeeper to play in the Champions League also produced a number of routine saves in a nervy finish.

This was a promising night for a fresh Villa era.

Full-time scenes in Bruges as Aston Villa get their Champions League campaign off to a winning start! 👏📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nYwtiQ6Xs7.

In a recent development, villa are defending with six at the back as midfield and defence merge into one. There are seconds remaining as Suzuki punts the ball up field and there is the final whistle! Villa make a winning start to the 2026-27 Champions League.

Another cross from the right is met, this time, by Tresoldi, but his header has no bite and Suzuki gathers.

Torres heads another Siquet cross behind for a corner. Brugge load the box but none of their players are able to get a meaningful touch on the ball before Diakhon slips just as he looks to get a shot away from the left of the box.

Slightly less mature play from Gomes, though. He bundles Vermant over and earns a needless yellow card.

Sources indicate that really mature play by Hemmings. Looking to break away, he simply puts his body between man and ball, inviting the challenge and winning a foul.

Villa are working hard in their compact mid-block and Brugge are struggling to find a way through.

Leko sends on Vermant and Diakhon for Potts and Virgili.

Sources indicate that barkley is one lucky boy. Attempting to play out under pressure, the midfielder gives the ball straight to Virgili, who cannot sort out his feet before offloading to Tresoldi far too late. A big let-off for Villa.

Gomes goes close after driving through Brugge’s midfield. He really should, though, have played in a free McGinn at the back post. Moments later Bogarde fires another shot goalwards but Sommer gets to it.

Abraham replaces goalscorer Jackson.

Sources indicate that villa have wrestled control away from their opponents. McGinn’s teasing cross evades everyone and Alysson’s cross takes a deflection which goes behind for a corner which is not up to much.

Lee hauls down Hemmings which gives Villa the opportunity to slow the game down. McGinn flights a delivery in from the left but Brugge clear their lines.

The ball comes out to Alysson who jinks in from the right, tiptoeing through a crowd, desperate to get a shot away on his left foot, but Seys does well to track his man and smother the effort.

Vanakan and Velesen and replaced by Tsawa and Lemarechal.

According to recent reports, yet another dangerous Siquet cross rains in from the right and here it is taken off Tresoldi’s toes by the tip of Lindelof’s boot. The defender did brilliantly to clear his lines at full stretch.

Hemmings burst towards the by-line and his cross trickles across the face of goal. Alysson is waiting at the far post but Seys does well to shield the ball and win a free-kick.

In a recent development, villa’s best chance at putting this game to bed will come on the counter. And here McGinn plays in Jackson whose one-vs-one effort is stopped by Sommer.

Virgili from the left, Siquet from the right. Threats are coming from both wings and Villa need to get their foot on the ball if they are to take the sting out of Brugge’s attack.

Instead they allow Vetlesen a yard of space and his long-range sighter stings the hands of Suzuki who turns behind for a corner.

Emery switches out Buendia, Kamara and Wan-Bissaka for Alysson, Barkley and Bogarde before the corner is taken, and Suzuki stops the eventual delivery on the line after the ball spun off the post!

Recent findings suggest that another Virgili cross threatens to carve Villa open but they just about clear their lines. Then it is Siquet who delivers, this time from the right, but his cross just evades Tresoldi and Mechele at the far post. Maatsen has a chance to break free but cannot build a head of steam before he is stymied.

Villa do appear pretty comfortable here, despite some frequent pressure from Club Brugge.

Recent findings suggest that it’s been a shocking night for Club Brugge’s upcoming goalkeeper Yann Sommer. Sources indicate that brugge have conceded just two goals in five league games this season, but their Pro League opponents have threatened against the Belgian champions’ right side, especially in attacking transitions. It has been revealed that christos Tzolis enjoyed an outstanding season with Brugge in 2025-26, contributing 51 goal involvements in 52 matches. His haul earned him a £34m move to Arsenal, where he has continued in much the same vein, laying on three assists in four matches.

According to recent reports, while Tzolis wears the No 17 at Arsenal, his former No 8 shirt at Brugge has been inherited by Englishman Freddie Potts, who made the move from West Ham to Belgium last month. One player to keep an eye on for Club Brugge is midfielder Freddie Potts.

Also in the Brugge team is Carlos Forbs, the former Manchester City trainee who had a poor loan spell at Wolves a couple of seasons back.
