In a recent development, mings is on the bench today. Matty Cash is out with a muscle issue so there is a first start for summer signing Aaron Wan-Bissaka.

According to recent reports, addressing the media in Monday’s pre-match press conference, Unai Emery was asked about the challenges of taking Aston Villa into another season in Europe with a significantly changed squad. He stated: “To continue in this level, changing some players, key players, but those key players we changed this year as well before the last year we were changing – not like this year, because this year was more players than normal, but we are replacing them.

According to recent reports, “We have the players with experience like here with Emiliano [Buendía] and they deserve to continue here trying take now more responsibility and try to give the players we have … Of course we have now new players with a lot of experience like Goretska for example, and we have some young players, they are coming from [major] clubs like Garnacho, Mbaye or Jackson. We must try to adapt them in our structure tactically and arrive [at that point] as fast as possible … We need time, I don’t know if we need time or not, it’s not for me something I’m thinking about, I am thinking about competing. To compete [in] each match.

According to recent reports, “We started the Premier League, the first competition, as our objective at the end of the season, because through it we can achieve our objectives this year, and we’re progressing. Still not enough, because we are not getting good results. But [the match against Brugge] is a upcoming test.”.

The experienced Yann Sommer starts between the sticks, with in-form striker Nicolò Tresoldi leading the line. English midfielder Freddie Potts is one of Ivan Leko’s two pivots.

Emery makes three changes from the XI that started against Hull City. Wan-Bissaka comes in for Matty Cash who does not make the match-day squad. Joao Gomes is eligible to play despite being suspended in domestic competition while Pau Torres replaces Tyrone Mings.

Aston Villa are back in the Champions League and in familiar territory with an unfamiliar team.

This will be their third match at the Jan BreydelStadion in less than two years but much has changed with the players that last competed here for Unai Emery.

Two of the goalscorers in the club’s last outing in Bruges were Leon Bailey and Marco Asensio, who are no longer at the club.

Of course, they are not the only players that have left and this is a latest-look Emery team hoping for lift-off this season.

Villa are the Europa League winners but this could be a tricky evening against the Belgian Pro League champions.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of Aston Villa’s Champions League opener against Club Brugge. Unai Emery’s side voyage across the Channel to face the Belgian champions having triumphed in last season’s Europa League and finished fourth in the Premier League. The Villa mothership has since sailed into choppy waters, though, with a raft of significant-name sales preceding a run of two defeats and a draw in the league. An opening-weekend thrashing by Brighton and Hove Albion proved quite the storm for Emery’s new-look crew.

Morgan Rogers alighted for Chelsea in a deal worth £117m, a record fee for an English player, and goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez followed soon after, while Youri Tielemans moved to Manchester United. Ezri Konsa and Ollie Watkins completed the exodus of leading men with late-August moves to Arsenal and Al-Hilal respectively. To remedy the outgoings, Villa twice broke their transfer record this summer, pipping Newcastle United to the signing of Johan Manzambi (£59.5m) before landing Nicolas Jackson (£65m, including add-ons), and added Taylor Harwood-Bellis and Ibrahim Mbaye on deadline day. Whether they can hit the ground running remains to be seen, but Emery has a task on his hands aligning his upcoming recruits before the scrutiny intensifies.

Although Villa swept aside Brugge 6-1 across two legs in the Champions League quarter-finals two seasons ago, here Blauw-Zwart (Blue-Black) represent a stern test having made the Jan Breydel Stadium a fortress in last year’s tournament. Their only home defeat in the league phase came against Arsenal, with a 3-3 draw against Barcelona backed up by 4-1 and 3-0 victories over Monaco and Marseille respectively. Belgium’s second-most decorated club have won seven of the last 11 league titles and know how to win matches. In Yann Sommer, Ivan Leko has one of world football’s most experienced goalkeepers, who kept the most clean sheets in the 2024-25 edition of the Champions League (seven). Captain Hans Vanakan, Brandon Mechele and Joaquin Seys were part of Rudi Garcia’s Belgium World Cup squad, and German striker Nicolò Tresoldi already has four goals in six matches this term. English midfielder Freddie Potts could also feature, having settled in nicely in West Flanders having moved from West Ham United during the summer.

The earlier 5.45pm kick-off time, means Villa, Brugge, LASK and AEK Athens have the opportunity to top the 36-team league …at least for a couple of hours.

Napoli Primavera, Nocerino: “Mi porto a casa la reazione. Dobbiamo avere una mentalità diversa”

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Antonio Nocerino, allenatore del Napoli Primavera, ha parlato dopo la sconfitta contro il Manchester City per 4-1 in Youth League:.
  • According to recent reports, “Siamo partiti male.
  • It has been revealed that club Brugge?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Antonio Nocerino, allenatore del Napoli Primavera, ha parlato dopo la sconfitta contro il Manchester City per 4-1 in Youth League:.

According to recent reports, “Siamo partiti male. Sembra che quando giochiamo queste partite si pensi di più a quello che c’è intorno, al rispetto per l’altra squadra, e non si pensi più a ciò che si deve fare in campo. Ai ragazzi per il secondo tempo ho detto di mettere ciò che avevano, di giocare, perché non avevano nulla da perdere, con coraggio e intensità. Abbiamo avuto delle opportunità, abbiamo preso una traversa, poi ci sono state delle situazioni a nostro favore che potevano essere finalizzate in maniera diversa. Mi porto a casa la reazione, l’approccio della ripresa, ovviamente sapendo anche contro chi abbiamo giocato. Va dato anche merito all’avversario, sono forti.

It has been revealed that club Brugge? Noi in tutte le partite vogliamo provare a fare risultato, anche lì, se dobbiamo chiudere, dobbiamo farlo nel migliore dei modi. Dev’esserci sempre quella speranza che non deve mai mancare. Dobbiamo giocarcela come sempre, l’obiettivo è fare bene e portare soprattutto in casa a vincere. È un sogno però ci vogliamo provare fino alla fine.

It has been revealed that campionato e Coppa Italia? Dobbiamo lavorare bene e recuperare le forze, oltre a mettere una mentalità un po’ diversa. Dobbiamo cercare di essere più aggressivi, vogliosi, più forti nell’uno contro uno e finalizzare un po’ di più quello che creiamo. Costruiamo tanto, arriviamo negli ultimi metri, ma abbiamo poca cattiveria nel chiudere l’azione. È una situazione secondo me individuale e mentale di ogni singolo giocatore. Noi alleniamo tanto i tiri e le situazioni di gioco, però poi c’è anche l’individualità del giocatore. Quando noi ti mettiamo in una condizione di tirare o di fare l’azione da gol, bisogna avere la cattiveria, la fame di fare gol. A noi manca un po’ questo. Finora siamo stati un po’ troppo ‘belli’, e in alcune situazioni dobbiamo essere un po’ più sporchi”.

Nel podcast Wes & Raf, l’ex centrocampista ripercorre il lavoro con il giocatore e la promessa di portarlo in Eredivisie.

Wesley Sneijder considera Tijjani Noslin un possibile convocato dell’Olanda, se continuerà il percorso che lo ha portato fino alla Lazio. Nel podcast olandese Wes & Raf, l’ex centrocampista dell’Inter ha ripercorso il lavoro fatto con il giocatore arrivato in Italia dal Verona.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

It has been revealed that sneijder ha ricordato come veniva giudicato Noslin prima dell’arrivo al DHSC: «Prima che arrivasse al DHSC, tutti lo consideravano un ragazzo molto difficile. Era un buon giocatore, ma molto complicato, mai puntuale…».

Per questo decise di parlargli e di stabilire con lui alcuni accordi. Dopo pochi allenamenti, racconta, si convinse che avesse le qualità per diventare un professionista: «Solo dopo qualche allenamento ho capito che aveva tutte le carte in regola per diventare un professionista.».

It has been revealed that sneijder vide in Noslin un potenziale enorme e iniziò a lavorare con lui. Gli promise che, se avesse rispettato gli accordi, lo avrebbe portato in Eredivisie. Il giocatore riteneva impossibile quel traguardo, ma l’ex centrocampista sostiene di aver mantenuto la parola nel giro di due anni: «Nel giro di due anni, l’ho portato davvero nel campionato olandese.».

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.
  • Published: 17:30 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 17:48 EST, 20 November 2026.
  • Martin O'Neill will weigh up replacing Mika Baur in the Europa League squad after the midfielder was ruled out for up to 10 weeks with an ankle injury.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 17:30 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 17:48 EST, 20 November 2026.

Martin O'Neill will weigh up replacing Mika Baur in the Europa League squad after the midfielder was ruled out for up to 10 weeks with an ankle injury.

The German hobbled off late on in Celtic's win over Kilmarnock almost a fortnight ago with a scan subsequently revealing that he sustained ligament damage.

One of the Parkhead side's star men since signing from Paderborn in the summer, Baur's absence is a major blow for O'Neill ahead of a defining period in the season.

While the manager will look to the likes of Oliver Sorensen and Joel van den Berg to step up domestically, he will also consider using a UEFA rule to make a change to his European squad ahead of Thursday's match away to Torreense in Portugal.

The rule allows clubs to make an alteration to the squad they submitted for the group stage if the injury is expected to sideline the player for more than 60 days from when it occurred.

Van den Berg, Jota, Landon Emenalo and Shim Mheuka weren't on the original 25-man list so would be options to be drafted in.

German midfielder Mika Baur could miss up to 10 weeks of action after injuring his ankle.

'I would definitely check with the medical staff and Mika, for a start,' said O'Neill.

Sources indicate that 'And speaking to him yesterday, he's really upbeat about it. Obviously, he will have that boot on for a few weeks.

'I suppose deep down, if it was, let's say, 10 weeks, that's taking you right through to the end of January. I can't see us seeing him in the next six weeks.'.

Baur's form following his £4.5million move has been good enough for him to win his first full cap for Germany after being called up by new manager Jurgen Klopp.

Industry observers note that 'He was doing great for us,' added O'Neill. 'It is a blow. And it seemed so innocuous at the time.

According to recent reports, 'I thought that he'd been kicked, but it was the other foot he'd landed on. It's just gone over. It's a real shame. He was playing great for us.

'There's things that he can't do for a while.'.

O'Neill revealed that Benjamin Nygren is also an injury doubt for Saturday's match with St Mirren.

Recent findings suggest that 'He didn't train today, but we'll see how he is in the morning,' he explained. 'He's got a sore heel. He missed out the second game in Sweden's run.

'He's been feeling it for a couple of weeks, so we'll see how he is tomorrow.'.

19-year-old summer signing Joel van den Berg could make his first Celtic outing this weekend.

Van den Berg hasn't played for the first team since joining from PSV Eindhoven for £3.4m in the summer with an injury impeding his progress.

But the 19-year-old could be in line for his first-team debut against the Buddies.

'I had a little chat to him,' remarked O'Neill. 'He trained this morning, he didn't train yesterday. We played a bounce game during the week, Tuesday against St Johnstone.

According to recent reports, 'He played in that game, came off and he was definitely limping for a while. He had a couple of days' treatment.

'In the overall scheme of things, whether it's tomorrow or in the next week or two, I'd hope to see him make his mark.

'As I noted to him yesterday, "When you get in, it's really up to you".'.

O'Neill anticipates a stern test from a St Mirren side who often have not picked up the positive results their performances have merited under Craig McLeish.

'The overall job he's done has been terrific, really terrific,' said the Celtic manager.

'They're having a wee tough time at this minute, obviously, with results, but his overall contributions, I'd say it's been excellent.

'There are some really fine coaches in Scotland, genuinely, and I don't want to sound patronising or sycophantic, but there are.

'We were up against one two weeks ago against Kilmarnock [Neil McCann], so I've got a lot of time for those boys who are coming through and who, to my mind, are every bit as good of coaches as quite a number down south.'.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

23.20 - Arcobaleno di Luis Milla, tanta garra in mezzo al campo e una resistenza opposta nel finale convulso dell'AEK Atene hanno permesso al Como di vincere 1-0. Cesc Fabregas, allenatore dei lariani, a breve parlerà in conferenza stampa. Diretta testuale a cura di TMW.

23.46 - Inizia la conferenza stampa.

According to recent reports, si aspettava di ritrovarsi a questo punto in classifica con 12 punti? "Ovviamente non mi aspettavo niente. Volevo solamente vedere come la squadra avrebbe reagito nella competizione più forte d'Europa. Poi siamo tutti motivati per la Champions e tre giorni dopo dimostrare quanto siamo forti. In questo momento se mi dici che a inizio stagione vinciamo 8 partite su 9 con 6-7 giocatori infortunati, con tanti altri fuori ruolo e che hai perso solo contro l'Inter ti avrei detto che sarebbe stato molto complicato. Penso che abbiamo meritato di vincere, abbiamo avuto tante opportunità, anche sbagliando un rigore. La competitività però nei 10-15 minuti alla fine, dove devi portare la vittoria a casa, con 4-5 cambiamenti e noi avevamo solo difensori. Sono molto felice. Non mi sono sentito inferiore a livello mentale in queste 5 partite".

TMW - L'ultimo club italiano capace di vincere le sue prime 3 gare interne di fila nella storia del torneo (Coppa dei Campioni inclusa) fu la Sampdoria (4 nella stagione 1991-92). E il Como ora... "Sappiamo che è un progetto speciale. Sono il primo che celebra 5 minuti e poi andiamo alla prossima. Se torniamo a tre anni fa, è vero, siamo cresciuti velocemente. Dobbiamo godercela almeno un attimo. Viviamo in un mondo che se perdi con il Frosinone ti ammazzano. Bisogna capire quello che sta succedendo, con umiltà e la voglia di lavorare. Si sta facendo una cosa diversa e speciale. All'esterno sembra una normalità. Quando sono arrivato quattro anni e mezzo fa, io ad allenare tre anni fa. Lo valorizziamo, piano piano, per ritrovare le forze. Voi scriverete che siamo meglio della Juventus, ma è la squadra più storica d'Italia. Noi dobbiamo trovare la forza per fare la partita perfetta un'altra volta".

Industry observers note that un'altra vittoria di misura, la prima in Champions però stavolta. "Contro il Milan e l'Inter ricordo 60-70 minuti grandi partite. Ho detto ai ragazzi di portare la sensazione di vincere e vincere a casa. Per il Como non è normale fare 8 vittorie su 9. Porta a casa questo fuoco, con una felicità assoluta. Bisogna valorizzarlo. Vincere è molto difficile nel calcio di oggi, si vede ogni weekend. Sono contento, anche della squadra come sta combattendo. Vediamo come si sviluppa la stagione per noi. Spero di poter recuperare dei giocatori".

In a recent development, decide lei e in base a cosa tra Sanchez e Butez in porta? "Sì, lo decido io se il presidente Suwarso non mi chiede un'altra cosa. Sono due portieri diversi, ma proviamo a trovare decisioni corrette. Sono due grandi portieri, ti possono dare tantissimo durante la stagione. Oggi mi aspettavo una, due o tre occasioni dell'AEK e ci sono state soluzioni per fermarli. Ho preso soluzioni giuste e vado a casa contento. Chalobah? L'altro giorno ho sentito Kempf e Ramon a un livello altissimo, per questo ho dato più tempo a Trevoh di fare più allenamenti. Oggi l'ho sentito bene, sapevo che non avrebbe potuto giocare 90 minuti".

Che status di allenatore si sente di avere a questo punto in Champions League? "Non lo so e non mi interessa molto. Non so cosa succederà in carriera, io sono felice di essere qua e di combattere tutti i giorni nel Como, con questo progetto e questa storia. Sono impressionato dai tifosi, come ci aiutano e come sono dietro la squadra. Il mio status di allenatore? La cosa che mi importa di meno. Per me c'è il Como, il Como e il Como. Se si deve sempre ammazzare qualcuno, che sia io. Io faccio questa carriera per passione assoluta. Il mio sogno è allenare il Como, era un'opportunità incredibile. Sono contento che succeda tutto questo, con un direttore giovanissimo come Ludi, con un direttore come Mirwan. Siamo una famiglia e dobbiamo continuare".

It has been revealed that da Cunha comincia a perdere lucidità? "No. Lucas non avrebbe dovuto giocare sabato con il Cagliari. O gioco io o gioca lui, quindi è successo così. Settantadue ore dopo deve mettersi la fascia da capitano e giocare in Champions League. Lo stiamo mettendo in una posizione dove non è perfettamente lui. Non possiamo giudicare tutto solo per il rigore. L'avesse fatto sarebbe stato MVP. Magari oggi Diao, Jesus Rodriguez e Addai sarebbe stato una festa di divertimento per puntare i terzini o con i cross dentro. Baturina e Douvikas hanno provato a fare il loro, e di Lucas sono contento. È un ragazzo d'oro".

Incide che ci sia una base di giocatori in questo Como. Si migliorano e sentono dentro di loro un sentimento di rivalsa nel vincere partite sporche. "Ne abbiamo parlato tante volte. Oggi la vita la vediamo che se non vinci sei scarso. Io non la vedo così. Quello che è successo a noi due anni fa, quando andavi a San Siro e facevi una partita incredibile e perdevi. Il processo lo devi sentire. A me ha fatto un male... non dormivo. Ma ti dà la forza di trovare soluzioni e continuare a spingere. So che ti aspettano per mesi, per dire questo e quest'altro. Dobbiamo vivere nel nostro globo per migliorare. Non importa quello che dicono fuori. Ma i ragazzi non si possono giudicare allo stesso modo con i vari Kakà e non solo. Ma questi ragazzi hanno fame, vogliono arrivare al top. Dopo sei mesi c'è una crescita. Jesus Rodriguez? Ha iniziato molto bene e poi ha avuto un calo. Ognuno ha il suo percorso e ognuno deve essere responsabile di capire come andrà. Abbiamo una visione con il presidente e con Ludi, vogliamo diventare una società stabile. La cosa più importante detta dal proprietario: valorizzare i giocatori. Non vincere. Penso che in questo momento stia andando bene, con uno stile di gioco e una cultura. Non possiamo dimenticare chi siamo".

In a recent development, milla e la fame di chi ha 32 anni e vive la sua prima Champions? "Questo mi dà più gioia di tutto. Vogliamo gente giovane e che vogliono fare sempre di più, poi c'è Milla. A 32 anni ha la gioia di tutti questi ragazzi giovani in un tempo diverso della sua carriera. Era felicissimo, non ha vinto 5 Champions e si vede dagli occhi quanto era contento. Questo mi fa godere. Un leader vero, molto importante".

00.09 - Finisce la conferenza stampa.

Newcastle scrape past Millwall to extend Jaissle’s unbeaten start

📅 08 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 24 min read (4842 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~24 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Joe Willock’s deft finish ensured Newcastle United survived a tough test against Millwall to keep their excellent run in the Carabao Cup intact.
  • This competition had been fruitful for Newcastle under former manager Eddie Howe and although this match was hard work – as well as hard to watch at times – his successor Matthias Jaissle guided them through a difficult trip to south-east London.
  • Recent findings suggest that he called it “job done,” and that was pretty much all it was.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Joe Willock’s deft finish ensured Newcastle United survived a tough test against Millwall to keep their excellent run in the Carabao Cup intact.

This competition had been fruitful for Newcastle under former manager Eddie Howe and although this match was hard work – as well as hard to watch at times – his successor Matthias Jaissle guided them through a difficult trip to south-east London.

Recent findings suggest that he called it “job done,” and that was pretty much all it was. “We needed patience on one hand, but also to be passionate and tough. We had the chance [to score] and took it,” he noted.

Newcastle have reached the semi-finals of this competition three times in the last four years, but struggled to get any sort of tempo going against their Championship opponents.

You could argue the winning goal came against the run of play late in the second half, moments after Millwall substitute Taïryk Arconte had smashed a low shot against the post.

"Livramento had a NIGHTMARE, he's so lucky" 😨Millwall were INCHES away from taking the lead against Newcastle 🤏 pic.twitter.com/X26aiTL432.

Sources indicate that given they were missing 13 players because of injury, this was a brave display from Alex Neil’s side. They frustrated Newcastle for more than an hour, nullifying their attack, to the point where Jaissle’s team looked as though they had run out of ideas.

That was until Lewis Hall combined with Matias Fernandez-Pardo down the left and his drilled cross found Willock who cleverly used the angle to pass the ball into the net. Willock has been rejuvenated under Jaissle. He looked certain to be sold this summer but is now starting regularly under a new manager in the number 10 role his system demands. It has been a nice redemption arc for the former Arsenal academy graduate.

In a recent development, moments after Millwall hit the post, Joe Willock strikes to put Newcastle in front! ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/rSB8yV6NRO.

The victory is all that matters and extends Jaissle’s unbeaten start to five games. Given he arrived just three weeks before the start of the season, that deserves praise even if it is obvious there is a lot of work to be done to improve their offensive play.

According to recent reports, playing in their lilac, or should that be Parma-violet, third kit for the first time, Newcastle looked off colour in the first half. Even though Jaissle named a strong team packed with experience of English cup ties, they struggled to overpower Millwall.

According to recent reports, there were a few half-chances as Willock forced a save and Jacob Murphy fired over. There was a header missed from a corner by Sven Botman, which should have hit the target and Yoane Wissa also mistimed his jump after finding space for another header.

Millwall’s two centre-backs, Jake Cooper and Caleb Taylor were immense, flinging themselves in the way of every shot and clearing every loose ball that came into their vicinity. Given their injuries, this was a performance full of fight and defiance from the home side.

However, there was also an absence of quality in the final third from Newcastle, the same lack of cohesion and incision that was apparent at home to Bournemouth last weekend and in the first half away at Tottenham Hotspur.

It meant Millwall were happy to play for set-pieces close to the Newcastle box and Taylor got in front of his marker, flashing a header wide of the post.

That lacklustre first half meant Jaissle’s side had mustered just five shots on target in five halves of football since the 3-2 win over West Bromwich Albion in the previous round of the Carabao Cup.

Millwall started the second period like a side sensing Newcastle were vulnerable. A thunderbolt from Jenson Metcalfe, after the visitors had struggled to clear two crosses, almost gave them a spectacular lead.

According to recent reports, newcastle saw lots of the ball. Millwall were happy enough to let them have it given how little they were hurting them.

So much of Newcastle’s play was slow and cumbersome. Their set-piece delivery was also largely inept.

Neil’s side retained a threat and came so close to taking the lead when, not for the first time, a long ball forward caught the Newcastle defence out of shape and Tino Livramento’s mistake allowed Arconte to run clear and hit the post from a tight angle.

Recent findings suggest that well in, @Joewillock! 💪 pic.twitter.com/5a8G7lzD3H.

Speaking after the game, Millwall manager Alex Neil said: “I’m very proud, I don’t think we deserved to lose that game.

“We had some good moments, and we got done by a bit of sucker punch at the end. But I’m very proud of the lads.”.

Recent findings suggest that as for their injury problems, he added: “I didn’t bring the teenagers on as a token gesture, I need to keep the first-team players fit. We’re really at bare bones.

But we beat Bolton at the weekend, got a couple of defeats before that but we started the season really well and once we get everybody back, we’ll be in good shape.”.

With the first of the 16 teams through tonight, the draw won’t take place until most of the teams have played next week.

It has been revealed that the draw will be shown on Sky Sports on Wednesday 16th Sept, after Manchester United play Brighton. Man City vs Norwich will be the only game outstanding then.

The third round had to be spread over two weeks as the nine Premier League sides in UEFA competitions entered the tournament in this round, as the same time as their Champions League and Europa League fixtures began. To avoid clubs facing clashes, the EFL split the fixtures across the two gameweeks.

It won’t go down in history as the greatest Carabao fixture, but Newcastle found a way to keep their momentum going and give Matthias Jaissle a win on his cup debut.

Newcastle aren’t taking any risks as Hornicek sends the ball long, and the players keep looking to send the ball down-field.

It has been revealed that seconds to go now. Marschall sends it long for one last effort, but it is cleared out of the box...

It has been revealed that willock has come off now for Newcastle’s own teenager, Sean Steur. A few more minutes and the man now on the bench with have done enough to send his side through to the next round.

We’re into the final minutes as Millwall are throwing everything at this.

Millwall are not out of this yet, as Neghli comes down the left side, twisting his way into the box past his defender – but having done the hard work, his shot flashes low across goal.

Some more changes, as Ramsey comes off for Newcastle, replaced by Lewis Miley.

A double change for the hosts as Dykes and Kelly come off for Regan Monty and Alfie Massey – the former just 15 years old.

Seconds later, another teenager takes to the pitch for Millwall as Osei-Tutu is replaced by 17-year-old Tristan Parkes.

Newcastle almost have another! From the sublime to the ridiculous, as Willock makes another run, this time down the left, and passes the ball onto the edge of the box where Elanga meets it in space. He lets it run, before taking his shot, but it is straight to Marschall.

Sources indicate that finally Newcastle have their breakthrough! They punish Millwall as Fernandez-Pardo feeds Hall on the left, who cuts inside and slips the ball across goal, finding Willock to redirect the ball to slot it home.

Marschall releases Arconte with a long ball and he turns Livramento to find huge amounts of space on the right side. He races into the box and takes a shot from close range, aiming for his near post, but is denied by the woodwork and the rebound hits the seated Hornicek. The keeper is lucky to not concede an own goal, as the ball bounces up and over his leg.

Sources indicate that issoufou again racing down the right side, before cutting inside and taking a shot with his left foot. Hall, who has been so crucial in the Newcastle attack, throws himself at the shot, and it flies high for Hornicek to collect.

Replays show that González, who Millwall players claimed had handled the ball earlier, leant down to clear with his shoulder.

Issoufou sends a great ball in for Millwall from the right side, but it is cleared by a Newcastle player, accompanied by cries for handball.

The game is opening up now as Newcastle make a run of their own, with Willock creating an opening for Elanga to take the ball to the edge of the box, before Taylor slides in to block his shot.

According to recent reports, millwall could absolutely win this with a smash-and-grab with less than 20 minutes to go. They are pushing for it but are lacking some attacking quality to finish the job.

From six shots they’ve had two on target, compared to Newcastle’s three on target from 20.

Fernandez-Pardo gets his first look at the ball, making a very quick run down across the centre of the field to the left side, but Osei-Tutu stays with him and takes him all the way to the back line before giving up a corner.

Elanga takes the corner, punched away by the keeper but no one goes to finish the job and Newcastle get another corner.

Metcalfe, who had his red card overturned this week, is the first player to go in the book for a mistimed challenge on Ramsey.

Just a reminder that there is no extra time, so if we’re all square after 90 minutes, it’s straight to a penalty shoot-out.

Willock gets the ball on the edge of the area and passes it on a quick turn to Barnes just inside the box, but there was not much on his shot and Marschall collects easily.

Sources indicate that double change now for Newcastle as Wissa and Murphy come off, replaced by Elanga and Fernandez-Pardo as Jaissle looks for pace. Schar is handed the armband.

It has been revealed that free kick for Newcastle, right on the corner of the box. Murphy takes, but it hits the wall 10 feet away, and bounces straight back to him. His cross into the box is headed out, and for all the opportunities Newcastle have created, they are yet to find the breakthrough.

We’ve also had a double change for Millwall as Esse and Lovelace have come off, replaced by Issoufou and Arconte.

It has been revealed that what colour would you describe this Newcastle away shirt? They look like the sweets Purple Violet to me. Although would you call it an all Lilac number?

In a recent development, it’s the first time they have worn their third kit. Not sure whether I like it or not. Shame The Den isn’t a sell out although I’m told tickets were priced at £31 and Millwall have a lot of injuries too.

Industry observers note that newcastle get another corner after a run from Willock. The delivery from Hall creates a good amount of confusion in the box and Marschall isn’t sure whether to stay on his line or come out to punch it away. From within the bodies, Wissa tries to get a shot off from close range but it bounces and the keeper easily collects.

González commits another foul, pulling down Esse, to give Millwall another free kick from 40 yards out.

The ball meets Taylor at the back post, but he meets it in the air and can’t quite direct it either into goal or back into the six-yard box, so it goes out for a Newcastle goal kick.

Another half chance for Millwall as Dykes feeds Kelly on the right side, who runs into the box and gets caught between passing the ball in and taking the shot, with the ball going high over the box.

Another great challenge from Osei-Tutu as Willock makes a run into the box, but is brought down by a well-timed tackle from the right-back.

The corner from Hall is better, but headed out and cleared.

Barnes again with space on the left side and he sends a ball fizzing low across the box to the far post but Neghli is able to lean on Murphy to stop him making contact.

Sources indicate that scramble for Newcastle as the ball is sent by Dykes to Neghli free at the far post, who puts the ball into a very dangerous area just in front of goal and everyone jumps on. Newcastle get to it first, managing to clear it from the goal mouth. It is cleared outside the box and it bounces to unmarked Metcalfe, who takes a thunderous shot, putting his laces through the ball but he is unable to keep it down and it goes over the bar.

Promising restart for the home side.

Despite Alex Neil’s premonitions, no changes for Millwall at the break.

Right-back change for Newcastle, as Dedic comes off and Tino Livramento comes on.

Leyton Orient 1-1 Bradford City.

And that’s the last action of the half, as just one minute was added on and that was taken up by Newcastle’s corner.

Nothing separates the two sides at the half, thought the visitors have dominated in terms of possession and chances.

Millwall have held fast and will be happy to be finishing the half level. We may see some changes from them after the break.

Sources indicate that the game is opening up before half-time, and Newcastle go again with Hall and Barnes. Osei-Tutu does well to wait before going in to block Barnes’s shot and send the ball behind for another Newcastle corner.

The delivery is once again poor, but Schar is pulled down inside the box by Taylor and is furious that nothing was given. There’s no VAR so there’s no review to consider – but looking at replays, Millwall were very lucky to get away with that foul.

Cooper makes a perfect pass down the left sideline, allowing Neghli to find space and forcing Newcastle to clear it away fo a Millwall corner.

The ball in is promising but Hornicek gets to it and punches it away, but the hosts keep the pressure on.

Baggott floats another ball across the box towards the right back post, but Hornicek easily collects the ball as Neghli can’t quite connect.

Recent findings suggest that newcastle moving the ball well again across midfield and it comes to Schar, who runs into space and gets a low shot away, around 40 yards out. It  takes a slight deflection on its way, going just wide of the post.

González is not having his best night and makes a silly foul against Dykes on the sideline, giving the hosts another set piece. The swinging ball in is not nearly as good as last time, and only reaches the first man, Newcastle’s Ramsey.

According to recent reports, millwall get a free kick, and the delivery is good, allowing Taylor to connect on the header inside the box. He beats Hornicek but the header rolls just wide of the post, to the groans of the home fans.

Hall goes short with the corner and Dedic has lots of time to cross the ball in from the right. It’s headed away but Millwall can’t break on the counter.

That sums up the game pretty well: not much finishing quality from Newcastle but Millwall not creating much from their limited spells of possession.

In a recent development, newcastle pushing again. Another ball pulled back by Barnes finds Ramsey at the top of the box, and his ball in connects with Wissa. Newcastle’s captain can’t head it in the right direction though and Millwall survive again.

The spell of pressure results in another corner for the visitors – and now we’re getting some pushing in the six-yard box.

According to recent reports, I think Millwall have done well. They have limited Newcastle to half chances and the odd set piece threat. They have made things really difficult for the visitors, crowding them out of space on the edge of the area.

When the home side have advanced up the pitch the Newcastle defence has not looked particularly secure.

As we reach the half-hour mark, Newcastle have 10 shots to Millwall’s one, though they sit one apiece on shots on target.

Esse gets caught on his heels as Hall pulls a long ball back on the left, and in the crowd at the top of the box Willock takes a shot, pulling it wide – cheers from the home crowd again.

First piece of good attacking play from Millwall as Neghli and Baggott work on the overlap. Baggott lofts a high ball to the back post, where Dykes gets a foot on it on the volley, but he can’t quite get over it and it’s easily picked up by Hornicek.

Barnes and Ramsey combine again down the left, with the midfielder trying to feed Barnes on his run. The pass has too much on it though, and as it runs out the back it’s met with jeers from the home fans for a goal kick.

It has been revealed that wissa breaks away down the centre of the field, with Barnes on his left, using him as a decoy. Wissa takes the shot though and it is blocked by a sliding defender.

It has been revealed that newcastle hit 20 minutes in with 68 per cent possession but nothing to show yet for their efforts. You feel like it will only be a matter of time though.

Sources indicate that another Newcastle corner, swung in well and Botman comes charging in, beating cooper to a free header. The defender heads it over the bar and holds his head in his hands. The visitors could definitely be a goal up by now.

Hall’s free-kick is met by the first man Metcalfe who heads it away to atone for his foul and Newcastle remain stymied.

Millwall will have expected Newcastle to dominate the ball but they are really pushing for an opener, especially down the left side with Barnes and Hall.

Again, Newcastle coming down the wings, this time on the left. Esse picks the ball up but loses it and Willock picks it up and takes a shot on his right foot with good power but sends it straight at Marschall. The debut keeper parries it away and it’s cleared by a  Millwall header.

Willock comes down the left soon after and is fouled by Metcalfe to get a free kick in a good spot outside the box.

Murphy gets a shot off after Dedic picks up a long ball on the right side and crosses it back towards the middle of the field. Murphy gets on it and takes the shot inside the box off his left foot but it sails over the bar.

González gives the ball away cheaply and Metcalfe picks it up, but unable to move it forward.

Newcastle will need to make sure they don’t get complacent in defence.

Millwall having a spell of possession, the counter-attack looking like their best option but as they move down the right hand side, Lovelace makes a late challenge to get the ball back and fouls Wissa.

Newcastle advancing, with Dedic and Ramsey moving the ball across midfield. Barnes gets the ball on the left of the box, and his ball is in knocked out and Newcastle get the first corner of the game.

Nothing comes of it as it is sent in high and long over the box.

Fair to say both teams are settling, but Millwall try and create a chance with Lovelace, though it’s intercepted. Dykes takes a bit of a knock and is slow to get up.

Newcastle have named a strong side – probably the strongest they could field when factoring in senior players needing game time – to take on Millwall in the Carabao Cup.

Jacob Ramsey impressed coming off the bench against Bournemouth last weekend and manager Matthias Jaissle refused to sanction winger Jacob Murphy’s transfer to Nottingham Forest late in the window. Both deserve a chance to impress from the start.

Veteran centre back Fabian Schar comes in for Malick Thiaw, but those are the only three changes from the side that drew with Bournemouth.

Jaissle insisted he would take the competition seriously and the teamsheet proves it, but it also raises questions about some of Newcastle’s summer recruitment.

Industry observers note that bazoumana Toure cost £42m but was withdrawn at half time in the win over West Brom in the previous round, which means Harvey Barnes does not get a rest. That’s a lot of money to spend on a winger who has not looked Premier League ready so far.

Sources indicate that aladji Bamba, a £30m signing from Monaco, has not started a game yet and has been an unused substitute since the opening game against Liverpool. He remains on the bench.

Even Sean Steur, who has looked good since his summer move from Ajax, cannot dislodge another more recent arrival in former Manchester City midfielder Nico González.

Having made a total of eight new signings in a much-vaunted summer rebuild, Jaissle only started three of them against Bournemouth and only two start tonight at The Den.

Early days but this was one of the main reasons Eddie Howe quit – he did not think the likes of Toure, Steur and Bamba were ready to play first team football.

Welcome to tonight’s live coverage of Millwall vs Newcastle United, as the Geordies travel to south London for the third round of the Carabao Cup.

Newcastle held off West Brom in their second-round match, with Harvey Barnes scoring two second-half goals to see his side through. It was a mighty comeback, after Isaac Price scored early to stun the crowd at St James’ Park. Bazoumana Toure equalised for Matthias Jaissle’s side just before half-time, and Barnes, his replacement in the second half, put them ahead minutes after the restart. West Brom pulled it back to 2-2 with a penalty converted by Price after Lewis Hall was deemed to have handled the ball in the box, but Barnes got his second just nine minutes from full-time and the hosts were able to see out the match to progress.

Alex Neil’s Millwall have reached round three via a 0-1 win over Cambridge United, following a penalty shoot-out in the first round to beat QPR. They come into this tie with a squad stretched thin, as they have been hit with an injury crisis a month into the newly introduced season. Millwall have confirmed that they will be without Casper De Norre, Josh Coburn, Tristan Crama, Alfie Doughty, Mathis Servais, Ryan Leonard, Mihailo Ivanovic, Lukas Jensen and Luke Cundle.

Both sides sit seventh in their respective leagues, with Millwall on a record of three wins and two losses this season, while Newcastle remain unbeaten (two draws and a win).

Newcastle will hoping to progress smoothly in a tournament that they have recently enjoyed good form in – winners in 2025 and semi-finalists last season – and with Millwall dealing with a bare bones squad, the Championship side are the underdogs on paper going into this fixture.

But, as always, anything can happen, so let us know your score prediction in the comments and we’ll be bringing you team news soon!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

L’ex direttore sportivo spera che il cammino biancoceleste duri tutto l’anno e vede i giallorossi in corsa fino alla fine.

Walter Sabatini non si aspettava di trovare Lazio e Roma ai primi due posti in campionato. L’ex direttore sportivo di entrambi i club elogia il lavoro di Gattuso con i biancocelesti e le qualità della squadra di Gasperini. Secondo quanto riportato da La Gazzetta dello Sport, Nella corsa allo scudetto, però, indica ancora l’Inter come favorita.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Sabatini, 71 anni, racconta anche delle proprie condizioni di salute dopo gli effetti delle migliaia di sigarette fumate: «Se senti un soffietto è perché ogni tanto mi attacco all’ossigeno, ma non ne avrei neanche bisogno».

It has been revealed that alla domanda se avesse previsto le due squadre romane in testa, Sabatini risponde parlando prima della Roma e poi della Lazio. Attribuisce a Gattuso un lavoro sbalorditivo nella preparazione emotiva dei biancocelesti: «No. Era chiaro come la Roma fosse una squadra meravigliosa, destinata a vincere ogni partita per la determinazione, l’autorevolezza, la convinzione che la rendono quasi imbattibile. Alla Lazio ha fatto un lavoro sbalorditivo Gattuso, che ha preparato emotivamente i suoi e giocatori l’anno scorso ai margini sono diventati protagonisti».

In a recent development, tra i giocatori cresciuti si sofferma soprattutto su Isaksen, dopo aver citato Belahyane e Noslin: «Penso a Belahyane, oggi invidiabile regista di copertura; a Noslin, attaccante che potrebbe giocare in qualsiasi club; a Isaksen soprattutto. Il danese ha sempre scontato una timidezza tecnica insopportabile. Le sue grandissime potenzialità le teneva nel cassetto, non prendeva rischi, adesso gioca in maniera prepotente, persino arrogante, può trasformare in oro qualsiasi situazione di gioco e questo è merito di Gattuso che ha lavorato sulla testa dei giocatori».

Industry observers note that per Sabatini sarebbe riduttivo identificare Gattuso soltanto con la grinta. All’allenatore affianca l’elogio del direttore sportivo Fabiani per le scelte di mercato: «Ha trasferito loro una parte del suo carattere, però smettiamola con la litania di Gattuso uguale Ringhio, solo grinta e basta. Stiamo parlando di un allenatore che fa giocare benissimo la sua squadra. Complimenti anche al direttore sportivo Fabiani, che è stato chirurgico sul mercato: ha preso quello che serviva e ha lasciato quello che non serviva».

Sabatini rifiuta l’idea che il percorso biancoceleste sia una favola: «Ma non è una favola. La Lazio è un fatto, una squadra autoritaria. Il mio augurio è che la storia della Lazio duri tutto l’anno».

It has been revealed that avendo lavorato come direttore sportivo per Lotito, Sabatini affronta anche il rapporto tra il presidente e i tifosi che lo contestano. Il suo giudizio parte dal riconoscimento delle qualità di Lotito: «È la magia del calcio, che restituisce quasi sempre quello che prende. Lotito è un grande presidente, lo dico con cognizione di causa. È dotato sotto il profilo temperamentale e della conoscenza calcistica».

According to recent reports, alla stima affianca però una critica sul coinvolgimento dei tifosi: «Sbaglia le cose facili perché sottrae a tutti, non so se involontariamente, il senso di partecipazione: i tifosi di ogni squadra si sentono i veri padroni del club, invece lui fa il presidente come gli pare, si prende tutto. Gliel’ho sempre detto ma non ha mai seguito i miei suggerimenti».

Sources indicate that il futuro di Matias Soulé potrebbe diventare uno dei temi caldi delle prossime sessioni di calciomercato. Le prestazioni del talento argentino con la maglia della Roma non sono passate inosservate, tanto in Italia quanto all'estero. Secondo quanto riportato dal portale tedesco Fussball News, sulle tracce del classe 2003 ci sarebbero Borussia Dortmund, Stoccarda e Atletico Madrid. Particolarmente nutrita anche la lista delle pretendenti in Premier League, dove il fantasista piace ad Arsenal, Newcastle, Sunderland, Aston Villa e Bournemouth. E - si legge - anche in Serie A Napoli e Milan avrebbero mostrato interesse con sondaggi con l'entourage del calciatore.

Sources indicate that la società giallorossa, forte di un contratto in scadenza il 30 giugno 2029, non ha necessità di accelerare eventuali trattative. La valutazione del cartellino di Soulé oscillerebbe tra i 55 e i 60 milioni di euro, una cifra importante che testimonia la considerazione del club capitolino nei confronti dell'argentino. Dal canto suo, Gian Piero Gasperini vorrebbe continuare a puntare sul talento dell'ex Juventus.

It has been revealed that A condizionare le strategie della Roma potrebbero però essere le esigenze economiche legate al rispetto dei parametri del Fair Play Finanziario. Un'eventuale proposta particolarmente vantaggiosa potrebbe dunque indurre la dirigenza giallorossa a fare delle riflessioni, nonostante la volontà dell'allenatore di trattenere il giocatore. Al momento non risultano offerte concrete sul tavolo della società capitolina e un eventuale trasferimento potrebbe concretizzarsi anche nell'estate del 2027.

#187349. Can Celtic boss Martin O'Neill muddle through until January cavalry arrives?

Can Celtic boss Martin O'Neill muddle through until January cavalry arrives?

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1272 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.
  • Published: 17:30 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 17:48 EST, 20 November 2026.
  • Although Celtic entered the international break on the back of victories over Besiktas and Kilmarnock, the upturn in results didn’t quite lead to an outbreak of unbridled joy along Kerrydale Street.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 17:30 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 17:48 EST, 20 November 2026.

Although Celtic entered the international break on the back of victories over Besiktas and Kilmarnock, the upturn in results didn’t quite lead to an outbreak of unbridled joy along Kerrydale Street.

Since the first act of this season, a narrow win over Dundee, Martin O’Neill’s side have occupied a place of uncertainty.

Those who have taken the occasional stellar display to be indicative of a corner being turned have been left feeling like fools.

Sources indicate that there remain too many shortcomings in the squad, too many question marks hovering above too many players to ever feel that it has left inconsistency behind. The fan base has good reason not to quite trust it.

How could it be otherwise when the clean sheet claimed against bottom side Killie was the first in seven matches?

Kasper Hogh, the club’s record signing at £11million, hasn’t scored in his last 16 outings in green and white.

Martin O'Neill admits it has taken longer than he'd have liked for the upcoming recruits to settle.

O’Neill’s options on the flanks include one player in Jota, who’s getting back from a long-term injury, and another in Yang Hyun-jun, who was recently sidelined for six weeks.

There’s a veteran in James Forrest, Seb Tounekti, not exactly the bravest of souls, and Haissem Hassan, a £6m signing who evidently believes defensive work is optional.

It claims much that Callum Osmand, a centre-forward now trying to cut it on the flank, has become a fans’ favourite after just 13 senior appearances.

The concerns of the manager now extend to the middle of the park where Mika Baur may be out for up to 10 weeks with ankle ligament damage.

With Benjamin Nygren also a doubt to face St Mirren, Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain, Luke McCowan and/or Joel van den Berg could be teamed up with skipper Callum McGregor.

We’re assuredly about to discover if this squad has more about it than the results and performances to this stage have suggested.

‘We can make significant improvements, there’s no question about it,’ stated the manager.

‘Top of the league, it is nice to be in that position. But other than a number of matches where I think we’ve played very, very well... maybe the Besiktas game, maybe the Hearts game, it’s been really hard work for us.

‘That’s maybe a combination of things. Young and slightly more experienced players coming into the football club, getting to know the club, getting to know the players.

It has been revealed that ‘That’s taken a bit of time. I didn’t expect it to work immediately overnight.

German midfielder Mika Baur is set to miss around 10 weeks with an ankle ligament injury.

‘But they’re at a club where settling in is something they’ve got to do pretty rapidly.’.

Starting with the visit of the Paisley men, Celtic have 10 games up to and including the trip to Ibrox on January 3.

That encompasses two assignments on the road in the Europa League — Torreense and Omonia Nicosia.

O’Neill’s men also visit Tynecastle, Dens Park, Pittodrie and Tannadice in the league.

As they prepare to put up the Christmas decorations on the Celtic Way, O’Neill could privately be forgiven for wishing the festive season away.

January 5 is the day on which the transfer window in Scotland opens and you can’t help but wonder what Celtic’s prospects for the season will look like at that point.

While Camilo Duran and Baur have contributed, the bulk of the business done in the summer again looks to have been sub-standard.

To stand a chance of retaining the title, O’Neill badly needs several substantial-hitters to come in without delay in the Upcoming Year.

Industry observers note that ‘We’re absolutely looking at players now,’ he stressed. ‘I suppose every single club is doing that. And the quicker you can get somebody in, the better.

‘We’ve seen when people are fit, we will have numbers. We just need a bit of quality.’.

Camilo Duran has been one of very few summer arrivals to have made an impact at Celtic.

Until such time as he can call for the cavalry, O’Neill has no choice but to make do and mend.

On the chances of prioritising the league and playing a weakened side in Europe, the veteran is clear.

‘Domestic football is really important to the football club, of course,’ he said. ‘But you’d still want to try and make some show in Europe. And we’ve found that difficult.

‘I genuinely thought against Besiktas we did really fine in the game, we didn’t over-press because they could play through you.

‘There are certain moments even in domestic football when teams can play through you. Kilmarnock caused us plenty of problems.

In a recent development, ‘I just think we’ve got to improve in the domestic games. We’ve got to be more aggressive in the sense of taking games to people and being less passive in periods of games.’.

O’Neill clearly needs more — much more — from so many individuals if he’s to get through the shark-infested waters of the next six weeks unscathed.

Hassan didn’t even make the matchday squad for Kilmarnock, a move which was interpreted by many as being a boot up the backside by a boss who’s been underwhelmed by his work without the ball.

‘We left out a number of players,’ O’Neill stressed. ‘I wouldn’t read as much into that, because a few will come back.

‘My job is not to please everyone, otherwise we’d have 26 players playing at one time.

O'Neill has backed misfiring striker Kasper Hogh to end his barren streak in front of goal.

‘I did a thing with corporate fans the other night, we had a bit of fun with some questions.

‘Apparently something came out that he [Hassan] was the most unpopular player in the dressing room, which is not true.

It has been revealed that ‘I didn’t say this. I was joking about my own unpopularity, as a player, because all I did was moan.

It has been revealed that ‘I did say about unpopularity, there’s at least one more unpopular. The crowd wanted to know but I didn’t tell them! I left it hanging. But it was tongue-in-cheek, apart from the part about me being unpopular, which I was.’.

The form of Hogh is no laughing matter. The Dane looked the part when he claimed a hat-trick at Kilmarnock on August 9, but that is beginning to feel like ancient history.

For his effort against the Ayrshiremen a fortnight ago to be ruled out for an earlier infringement by Baur was a low blow.

Industry observers note that ‘For him, that was a killer,’ O’Neill reflected. ‘He has got the goal, gone off and celebrated and you just think... oh no, is that a goal?

‘He has worked exceptionally hard for us. But strikers live by goals and at some stage or other, he needs a goal.

‘The best thing for me to do is bring Henrik Larsson over and show him how to hit the ball into the net.

‘Shaun Maloney was telling me that for a little period he played up front when Henrik was injured for about a month.

‘And Henrik in that time was giving him advice about how centre-halves were reading him. He told him about getting yourself room, losing the centre-half, don’t be fighting with him all the time.

‘He scored a bag full of goals, so there must be something in it.’.

In a recent development, le difficoltà difensive di questa prima parte di stagione hanno riacceso i riflettori sul reparto arretrato dell'Inter e sulla necessità di un ulteriore colpo in quella zona di campo da mettere a disposizione di Cristian Chivu. A tal proposito, secondo TMW, il nome giusto potrebbe essere Jeltsch dello Stoccarda, avversario domani dei nerazzurri in Champions League:.

"Finn Jeltsch sfiderà l'Inter in Champions League e chissà, magari quella di domani sera sarà solo la sua prima partita, di tante, che giocherà a San Siro. Il difensore classe 2006, di nazionalità tedesca e di proprietà, appunto, dello Stoccarda è entrato nel mirino della dirigenza nerazzurra anche in vista del prossimo mercato di gennaio, nel quale, con molta probabilità, il club campione d'Italia in carica andrà alla ricerca di un centrale che possa sistemare le cose nel reparto arretrato, troppo spesso in apnea in questa prima parte di stagione".

"Il problema numero uno relativo alla possibile operazione per portare il difensore a Milano è rappresentato dai costi. Il ventenne, che ha già esordito in Nazionale nonostante la giovane età, lo scorso 16 novembre nella vittoria dei tedeschi per 5-0 contro l'Olanda, ha infatti fatto lievitare settimana dopo settimana il costo del suo cartellino, arrivato oggi a circa 40 milioni di euro. Troppi per l'Inter, specialmente per gennaio. Per questo il discorso potrebbe essere rimandato a giugno, quando magari il club nerazzurro avrà un budget diverso".

  • Sources indicate that nel suo racconto, la motociclista ha riferito che stava viaggiando sotto la pioggia e aveva rallentato in prossimità di un incrocio.

In a recent development, vampeta è stato coinvolto in un incidente stradale nel quartiere di Vila Maria, nella zona nord di San Paolo. In un'intervista rilasciata a SBT, l'ex Inter ha negato di aver tentato di allontanarsi dal luogo dell'incidente e ha assicurato di non aver bevuto alcolici. Inoltre, l'ex giocatore ha raccontato di aver consegnato 500 real alla donna per aiutarla a sostenere le spese per i pezzi di ricambio della moto, ma che successivamente lei avrebbe chiesto una somma maggiore.

�Stavo giocando a calcio al club con i ragazzi e stavo tornando a casa. Percorrevo una strada piena di incroci. Pioveva e l'asfalto era bagnato. Sono passato con la macchina e una moto è caduta. Non sapevo nemmeno che alla guida ci fosse una ragazza. Mi sono fermato 20-30 metri più avanti e sono arrivati quattro motociclisti che fanno consegne. Uno di loro ha detto: "Questo ha i soldi". La ragazza non ha detto nulla. Quel tizio mi ha fatto perdere la pazienza. Sono tornato indietro, la ragazza era ancora lì, è arrivata una pattuglia e ho chiesto subito di fare la denuncia», ha raccontato Vampeta.

Sources indicate that nel suo racconto, la motociclista ha riferito che stava viaggiando sotto la pioggia e aveva rallentato in prossimità di un incrocio. In quel momento, secondo la sua versione, l'automobile guidata dall'ex calciatore sarebbe sopraggiunta ad alta velocità. Nel tentativo di frenare, avrebbe perso il controllo della moto, finendo per urtare la parte posteriore laterale della vettura. La donna, che lavora come corriere, ha inoltre dichiarato che la ruota della moto avrebbe colpito il suo casco, provocando la rottura della visiera e danneggiando anche lo specchietto retrovisore. Dopo l'impatto, Vampeta avrebbe parcheggiato alcuni metri più avanti, ma, secondo la versione della donna, avrebbe tentato di lasciare il luogo dell'incidente prima dell'arrivo della polizia. Alcuni motociclisti presenti nelle vicinanze sarebbero intervenuti, impedendogli di allontanarsi.

La donna ha infine sostenuto che l'ex calciatore mostrasse un comportamento compatibile con uno stato di ebbrezza e che si sarebbe rifiutato di sottoporsi all'alcoltest. La dinamica dell'incidente e le versioni fornite dalle persone coinvolte presentano dunque delle divergenze e dovrà essere la polizia a ricostruire l'esatta dinamica.

Mercoledì 25 novembre alle 15 il capitano biancoceleste sarà nella scuola primaria di via Monte Zebio 35. L’incontro arriva dopo la decima vittoria in dodici giornate della squadra di Gattuso.

Dopo qualche anno di pausa, la Lazio torna nelle scuole di Roma e per il primo appuntamento sceglie di presentarsi con il suo capitano. Mercoledì pomeriggio, grazie ad un'iniziativa di Sport e Salute insieme ad Adidas contro il drop out nello sport, sarà il capitano della Lazio Mattia Zaccagni a incontrare gli alunni della primaria Pistelli. Per i bambini che la domenica lo seguono dagli spalti o davanti alla televisione, stavolta l’indirizzo da ricordare è quello che conoscono meglio, quello della loro scuola.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

C’è un dettaglio che rende speciale il pomeriggio di via Monte Zebio. Di solito sono i più piccoli ad accompagnare i calciatori sul prato prima del fischio d’inizio. Mercoledì le parti si invertiranno e saranno gli alunni ad accogliere Zaccagni nel luogo in cui trascorrono le loro giornate. Al capitano il compito di rappresentare anche i compagni in questo ritorno tra i banchi romani.

Industry observers note that L’appuntamento cade in un momento felice per i colori biancocelesti. La squadra di Gennaro Gattuso ha appena centrato la decima vittoria nelle prime dodici giornate di campionato, un passo da record che racconta con quanta continuità la Lazio stia raccogliendo risultati. È questa la squadra che Zaccagni porterà idealmente con sé alla Pistelli. Per un pomeriggio, il volto di quella corsa in campionato sarà a pochi passi dai bambini che per lui fanno il tifo ogni domenica.

Tra i retroscena più curiosi di Manchester City-Napoli, terminata 2-2 all’Etihad Stadium, c’è stato il gesto di Erling Haaland nei confronti di Gianluigi Donnarumma. Minuto 44: sugli sviluppi di un corner battuto da Politano, Beukema trova il tempo per colpire di testa da distanza ravvicinata.   • Tottenham star Tosin Adarabioyo has joined forces with former Chelsea team-mates Reece James and Levi Colwill to launch a trading card shop in London.
  • Card Cop, opening in Borough Market on Thursday, will sell cards from a variety of sports as well as other collections such as Pokemon and Marvel.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 18:00 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 18:06 EST, 20 November 2026.

Tottenham star Tosin Adarabioyo has joined forces with former Chelsea team-mates Reece James and Levi Colwill to launch a trading card shop in London.

Card Cop, opening in Borough Market on Thursday, will sell cards from a variety of sports as well as other collections such as Pokemon and Marvel.

Sources indicate that adarabioyo began collecting as a child and returned to the hobby in 2020. His collection, which he shares on social media, spans a variety of sports and he also has several of Brazilian icon Neymar.

'I’ve been collecting for years, and it’s great to see the hobby continue to grow,' said the 29-year-old, who left Chelsea for Spurs last summer.

'I love collecting. It’s a great way for supporters to connect with their favourite players. I’ve always felt that collectors are some of the most passionate fans.

Industry observers note that 'I’ve got to know so many collectors through the hobby. Talking about our collections is an instant icebreaker, and I know those conversations can mean a lot. I want to bring more players into the hobby and recreate those moments.

Tosin Adarabioyo, like many footballers, has a passion for collecting trading cards.

The new shop is set to open in London's Borough Market next week.

Adarabioyo enjoyes collecting cards of former PSG star Neymar, who won 130 caps for Brazil.

According to recent reports, 'Neymar is criminally underrated to me, and I think his cards are too. Some of the images take me straight back to performances I’ve watched over the years. It’s hard to describe, but it’s like bottling up that feeling forever. Football purists will know what I mean.'.

West Ham defender Kyle Walker-Peters, who played with Tosin at England youth level, is among backers along with James and Colwill.

Adarabioyo already has an online retail business, The Huddle, with guests such as Dominic Solanke, Robert Sanchez and Adam Wharton all featuring on live streams, opening boxes as fans watch.

Recent figures valued the global sports trading card market at $13.75billion (£10.5bn) in 2025, with that projected to grow to $27.52bn (£21bn) by 2034.

Formula One star Lewis Hamilton got in on the act earlier this year, launching his own venture and a shop in Frankfurt.

The seven-time world champion was already an ambassador for Topps - who also have the licence for Premier League cards - and said: 'I’ve loved collecting cards since I was a kid — Pokemon, football, anything I could get my hands on.

'To now play a role in shaping the future of the category is incredible. We have a significant opportunity to tap into the culture in a way no one has before.'.

Man City survive tunnel clash and Porto fury thanks to Haaland double

📅 08 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 26 min read (5252 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~26 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Erling Haaland revealed on the eve of this clash how he loves chopping firewood in his spare time – and his goals set alight Manchester City’s Champions League campaign on a fractious evening in Porto.
  • Sources indicate that so much for the new group stage of the competition taking time to warm up.
  • Industry observers note that and City were not easing themselves back into European action either, they went full throttle at the start of a tough set of group games.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Erling Haaland revealed on the eve of this clash how he loves chopping firewood in his spare time – and his goals set alight Manchester City’s Champions League campaign on a fractious evening in Porto.

Sources indicate that so much for the new group stage of the competition taking time to warm up. This clash was a hot-blooded, bitter contest that spilt over in the tunnel at half-time, with players getting separated and tempers rising.

Industry observers note that and City were not easing themselves back into European action either, they went full throttle at the start of a tough set of group games. With Enzo Maresca, it looks like it will be all-out attack to get the best out of this team.

They can look nervous at the back, particularly with the ball at Gianluigi Donnarumma’s feet, but have attacking weapons to hurt any team in this elite competition. This was a performance that their rivals will take note of.

“It was a complete performance on and off the ball for 95 minutes,” was Maresca’s assessment.

City will certainly scare the traditional heavyweights with Haaland leading their attack and taking an axe to Porto’s defence like he does with logs in his back garden. It was his 58th and 59th goal in 59 games in the Champions League, with his latest an expertly directed header off a post and a calm side-footed finish.

NO MISTAKE from Erling Haaland this time 💪He's put Man City 1-0 up in Porto 🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/UpKOqQA49s.

Industry observers note that there is an argument that Pep Guardiola could have achieved more in the Champions League, given City’s dominance in domestic football. They have been knocked out by Real Madrid in the last three seasons but this is a new City, different personnel and even a new look.

According to recent reports, they wore their black and yellow away kit, inspired by “Manchester’s iconic worker bee” according to Puma, and grafted their way to victory here. Non-stop running going forward, and scrapping with Porto, too.

The Portuguese champions were not happy with Marc Guéhi’s challenge on Gabri Veiga and claimed an elbow was used, with the row carrying on in the tunnel at half-time with security guards separating the players. Rúben Dias also appeared to nudge a Porto official on his way to the dressing room.

According to recent reports, “I didn’t see anything but anyway, you can ask how many times you see me or my bench stand up? Zero, for 95 minutes. How many times do you see their bench? So...” Maresca added.

Only Dias and Haaland remain from the starting line-up from the Champions League triumph three years ago, so this is essentially a newly introduced team with a new manager.

Erling Haaland seals the deal in Porto 🤝🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/10xSTtZ8nw.

Phil Foden, on as a sub in that game, started at Estádio do Dragão after his horse Wreck It Ronnie defeated Najidi Storm, which started the Goodwood race with 1-33 odds and is now the shortest-priced loser in British racing history. The rest of the team are new to City’s challenge.

That includes Ayyoub Bouaddi, 18, who was part of a £320m midfield refresh following the departure of Rodri, who was named among the Ballon d’Or nominees a few hours before kick-off to highlight the experience and class City have lost.

In a recent development, bouaddi, who cost £81.4m from Lille, made a good start in his full debut. The Moroccan teenager is neat on the ball and gets around the pitch, with the next step being able to dominate games like his predecessor.

Sources indicate that “In his last game he lost two balls and stayed calm and was back in our box,” Maresca noted. “This demonstrates how good he is because any player after two [poor] passes panics, but he is just 18. Erling, Rúben, Mateo [Kovacic], they can manage these kind of games better, but you don’t expect it from a guy of 18. I didn’t see him panic.”.

Sources indicate that by Bouaddi’s side in midfield was Enzo Fernández, who sought to drive forward into space when City counter-attacked. He was among the players who, along with Dias, were reminded of their Benfica history by the home fans.

Industry observers note that diogo Costa tends to be linked with a move to the Premier League every summer, but has been a one-club man for his career so far. But he showed why clubs are looking at him with his first-half saves to deny Haaland and Rayan Cherki.

Porto’s legendary goalkeeper, Helton, was in the press box at half-time and would have been impressed with the saves, although he was not in his seat when Haaland scored the first goal, which came 94 seconds after the restart.

In a recent development, city had worked the ball around the penalty area, with Antoine Semenyo drawing out Costa before laying off to Fernández. Haaland’s header from the cross had such precision that the goalkeeper did not dive as it angled in off a post.

Still, Porto had their chances with Alberto Costa heading wide from a corner and William Gomes charging down a Donnarumma kick – with City’s most nervous moments coming when they passed around their back line.

It has been revealed that man City are living dangerously here! 🫣Donnarumma nearly gifts Porto an equaliser 😬 pic.twitter.com/otIfZTHmdn.

But Haaland sealed the win as the game ticked into stoppage time, finding the bottom corner from Rayan Aït-Nouri’s cutback.

“It was an amazing game against the champions of Portugal. We knew it would be a difficult fight, man against man, they are a top team,” Haaland remarked. “They play amazing football. All the pressure, we have to deliver on the big stage and that’s what we did. We controlled the whole first half, created chances.”.

Sources indicate that for Maresca, the victory was also a challenge against Porto’s aggression, with the Italian coach adding: “I was very pleased. We know in this kind of game when you come here it’s always difficult or tricky. The environment, the way they grew up, it’s normal, but I think we dealt with that very good.”.

Top performance, Enzo 👊✨ pic.twitter.com/ds0f207tpS.

Man City have now won seven of their last eight opening matchdays in the UEFA Champions League 🔵Starting strong 💪 pic.twitter.com/CIjsMj4Dig.

In a recent development, “I think we could have scored more goals, especially in the first half. We overall deserved the win and happy with the performance. If you think you can come to a place like this and play and not concede any chances, that is not realistic and it is normal. I am quite lucky as I have a squad of good players. It is a special competition and all the games are very difficult. He [Ayyoub Bouaddi] never panicked and was very good. The performance from him was unbelievable. I am happy to reunite with Enzo [Fernandez], who was very good.”.

36 - Erling Haaland scored his 36th UEFA Champions League goal for Manchester City, equalling Sergio Agüero as joint-most for the Citizens in the competition.Inevitability. pic.twitter.com/HHbNadybxh.

“I am so happy with how my teammates have welcomed me into the club. They are not just great players but great human beings. The fans have been absolutely brilliant and this is a new step in my career. Erling [Haaland] is an animal, a beast. Every time I am on the pitch, I will look for him and look to assist him. He is an amazing human being and helped me settle in. I am happy Enzo [Maresca] did all he good to make the move happen. I am so grateful for everything he has done for me and my family.”.

5️⃣9️⃣ appearances 5️⃣9️⃣ goals@Erling's #UCL record 🤯 pic.twitter.com/v6IvpwC9vm.

“Amazing game against the champions of Portugal. We knew it was going to be a tough game, they play amazing football. We had to deliver on the biggest stage and we did. We controlled the whole of the first half. We created a lot of chances. They pushed us for a good 25 minutes in the second half but we pulled through. These are the games we have to win. We have had a great start to the season.

Sources indicate that “He [Ayyoub Bouaddi] had a really good game and he has been amazing in training. I think we have a gem there. We have to learn and Enzo [Maresca] demands a lot from us. We demand a lot from each other. It was an unreal atmosphere so I hope Enzo is happy with that.”.
