The final whistle is blown and Manchester City begin their Champions League campaign with a 2-0 win in Porto. Erling Haaland’s double gives Enzo Maresca a victory in his first Champions League game in charge of Manchester City.

Industry observers note that enzo has two shots from range in quick succession, one from a free-kick. The free-kick goes just wide and the second is saved by D Costa.

In a recent development, it has been an ill-tempered game and tempers have boiled over again. Rosario and Haaland are involved in a tussle on the floor, which then leads to a mass melee. Haaland and Rosario are both booked for their part in starting that. Haaland is pleased that he got booked but I am not sure why. Both played their part in that melee.

It has been revealed that enzo Maresca’s side will head home with all three points. Ait-Nouri’s cross from the left side of the box picks out Haaland, who first-time shot from 10 yards out picks out the far corner. A clinical finish from Haaland and Manchester City will start their Champions League campaign with a win.

Erling Haaland seals the deal in Porto 🤝🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/10xSTtZ8nw.

There will be five added minutes.

Industry observers note that that is really poor refereeing. Porto are denied two clear fouls before Rosario is then punished for a foul on Enzo, which was a foul but so too were the previous two incidents. Francesco Farioli is then booked for his protestations but you can understand their frustration.

Ait-Nouri has the chance to warp up the three points with an effort from the edge of the box but his shot with his weaker right foot goes narrowly wide.

Nothing comes from the corner as Hwang’s delivery to the front post is dreadful.

Haaland has his fourth headed chance of the game but this one goes over the bar from Ndiaye’s cross. Haaland has scored one of those chances but spurned some good ones.

Down the other end, Fofana, only just on, wins Porto a corner and whips up the home fans.

A final change of the night for Porto sees Fofana replace Veiga. One last roll of the dice from Francisco Farioli.

Whilst Manchester City’s lead is only 1-0, Porto will believe an equaliser is there for them. However, the momentum they were building 10/15 minutes ago has seemingly been lost and the visitors have managed to wrestle back a bit more control.

That is a big chance missed by Pepe. Gimenez receives it down the left and pings a cross to the back post. The cross perfectly picks out Pepe, who fluffs his lines and completely mis-kicks.

Sources indicate that manchester City are making their final two substitutions of the night as Kovacic and Ait-Nouri come on for Bouaddi and Foden. Ait-Nouri looks like he is going to play left wing.

Two more changes for Porto as Silva and M Fernandes are replaced by Gimenez and Moura.

Porto are going to make their first two changes of the night as Hwang and former Norwich man Sainz come on. Varela and Gomes head off.

It has been revealed that for the second time in the half, Donnarumma is lucky. To be fair to the Manchester City keeper, the pass back to him is poor but he is then fortunate. His attempted ball out to his left is intercepted by Gomes but it rolls behind for a goal kick. That ball could have rolled straight into the Manchester City net or fallen straight back at Gomes feet with an empty net ahead of him. Donnarumma was very lucky on Saturday against Coventry to avoid a calamitous moment and he is lucky to avoid another awful moment for the second time in quick succession.

According to recent reports, man City are living dangerously here! 🫣Donnarumma nearly gifts Porto an equaliser 😬 pic.twitter.com/otIfZTHmdn.

Sources indicate that ndiaye receives it out on the left before driving inside. He gets his shot away from the edge of the box and tries to pick out the far corner but it is too close to D Costa and an easy save for the Porto keeper.

A fine pass from Rosario inside his own half cuts through Manchester City’s midfield sends Varela racing through the Manchester City half. He plays it out to his right to find Gomes, who cuts inside onto his left before trying to beat Donnarumma at his near post but the shot goes wide.

Recent findings suggest that enzo Maresca responds to a shift in momentum in this game making a double change. Anderson and Ndiaye come on for Cherki and Semenyo.

Porto have started to gain some momentum and they want a penalty. Bouaddi is perhaps a touch fortunate not to be penalised for a foul right on the edge of the box but it may have been just outside the penalty area. You can feel the game starting to turn in Porto’s favour.

Industry observers note that varela is inches away from an equaliser for Porto and plenty of the home fans thought the ball was in the net. Varela sends a curling effort towards goal from the edge of the box but it goes narrowly wide.

According to recent reports, that was a glorious chance for Porto to equalise. A corner is sent in from the left to the back post, where Alberto heads it back across goal. However, none of his teammates, including Silva, could tap the ball into the net. Porto should probably be back on level terms.

Donnrumma is a very, very lucky man. Porto would have had a certain penalty as Donnarumma completely flattened Pepe but the latter was offside so it is no penalty. Donnarumma has been booked but avoids a penalty, which would have been a guarantee had Pepe been onside.

Just three minutes into the second half, Enzo Maresca has made a substitution. Gvardiol, on a yellow, is withdrawn and Khusanov is brought on.

Porto’s legendary goalkeeper, Helton, was embracing Daniel Sturridge in the press box and they weren’t in their seats when the goal went in. Lovely move from City and Haaland steered in his 58th goal in the competition.

Erling Haaland moves 7th in the ALL-TIME UCL top-scorers list 💪🇳🇴📊 pic.twitter.com/oIkrPxm0gT.

According to recent reports, haaland wasted two headed opportunities in the first half but he does not spurn this chance. It is a first Manchester City assist for Enzo, who clips in a cross from the left side of the box. Haaland meets it and his header glances off the far post and goes in.

NO MISTAKE from Erling Haaland this time 💪He's put Man City 1-0 up in Porto 🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/UpKOqQA49s.

Recent findings suggest that gabriel Clarke on Amazon Prime has reported that there was some trouble in the tunnel as the two sides went off for half-time. Both sets of security teams for the clubs were forced to step in.

We are back under way in Porto. Tempers were really starting to boil over as that first half wore on so will that continue into the second half?

It has been revealed that the former Liverpool, Manchester City and Chelsea striker has described the incident involving Marc Guehi and Gabri Veiga as a “nasty collision” and “it does not look good at all”. I think Guehi is a lucky man to still be on the pitch as some VAR officials would surely have recommended a review for that foul. Porto boss Francesco Farioli felt Guehi led with his elbow and the home fans were not happy with that as well as a number of other decisions in that first half.

The first half is brought to an end and tempers are flaring as the two sides head off, with the game level at 0-0 at the break. The Porto fans and players are not happy with the officiating and Enzo is also involved in some antics.

Gvardiol needs to be careful as he is not punished for delaying a restart when you consider he is already on a booking. The Porto fans want to see a second yellow but the referee notes the ball was moving so Porto could not take the restart.

Three added minutes to conclude this first half.

According to recent reports, should Guehi be in trouble here? He appears in real time to win his header but when you watch the replays he led with his arm. He catches Veiga right in the face and Guehi could be in some strife. However, VAR is not going to take any further action and Guehi can count himself lucky. The medics are on to tend to Veiga and you do wonder why VAR has not recommended a review. The ridiculous thing about that was that Guehi was not punished with a yellow card or even a free-kick. That clearly indicates the referee did not properly see it.

According to recent reports, porto fans quick to remind Ruben Dias and Enzo Fernandez of their Benfica history. They jeered the pair when they got on the ball. Enzo is getting it from all angles at the moment, with Coventry fans taunting him at the weekend. He can expect more of that in the Premier League after his part in England’s exit at the World Cup, which led to Argentina players holding up a flag saying the Falkland Islands were Argentina’s.

It has been revealed that tensions are boiling over. They have been threatening to do so between Gomes and Gvardiol for a little while and now they do. Gomes steals the ball off Gvardiol and attempts to counter but is pulled back by Gvardiol, who is rightly booked. Gomes is not happy with Gvardiol and they come to blows.

In a recent development, D Costa twice denies Manchester City in a matter of seconds. First he saves from Haaland, then gets to his feet to deny Cherki. Manchester City are knocking on the door and you do feel like a goal is coming for Enzo Maresca’s side.

No goals in Porto but Real Madrid have their second at home against Inter Milan through Fede Valverde.

Manchester City struggled to carve out any genuine chances in the opening quarter of an hour but there are creating more and more opportunities, the latest falling to Foden, whose shot from the right side of the box looking for the far corner is saved by D Costa.

Industry observers note that it is not often you see Haaland miss two good chances with his head in quick succession but that is what has happened. Semenyo cuts inside on the left onto his right and curls in a cross into a good area. He picks out Haaland but the Norwegian’s header misses the target. He knows he should have done better as he shakes his head in frustration.

Porto’s front three have struggled to have much of an impact in the game, in particular Silva up top, who has been almost non-existent.

A great save from D Costa to deny Haaland. Foden’s cross just before the byline on the left side of the box picks out Haaland. The Norwegian has barely touched the ball tonight but comes close to opening the scoring. However, D Costa is on hand to deny him with a fine save. Should Haaland have given D Costa the chance to save it? Maybe not.

Industry observers note that in probably the marquee match-up of the night, Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid are taking on Inter Milan at the Bernabeu. Real have just taken the lead through Kylian Mbappe.

Semenyo cuts inside from the left and gets a shot away from the edge of the box but it is straight at D Costa. That was Manchester City’s first shot of the night.

It has been revealed that veiga has a shot saved at the near post by Donnarumma but the offside flag goes up. Veiga and Pep exchange a neat one-two down Porto’s left before Veiga’s effort is saved but Pepe was offside in the build-up.

Manchester City are dominating possession and perhaps it was a ploy by Enzo Marecsa to take it slowly and hog the ball in order to take the early sting out of Porto. The visitors would have been expecting the hosts would want to start hot so maybe they were willing to be slow on the ball in order to quieten down the crowd early doors. They have not had a shot yet and not really threatened the Porto goal but the hosts have not offered much going forward.

The weather in Porto really is horrible, the type of weather you would expect in Manchester in mid-November than Porto in early September.

Recent findings suggest that porto have a strong defensive record thus far this season but undoubtedly they will be tested a lot more tonight than they are in Liga Portugal. You would also imagine they will have to be clinical in attack as they are unlikely to create as many chances as they do domestically.

It has been revealed that with it hammering down, Porto boss Francesco Farioli has swapped his lovely suit that he was wearing pre-game for a tracksuit top and cap. At half-time, he will probably head back in drenched like all the players if he is active in his dugout.

We are under way at the Estádio do Dragão with the rain still teaming down in Porto. Manchester City’s Champions League campaign gets going.

It has been pouring down in Porto but that has not dampened the spirits of the home fans, who are in fine voice ahead of kick-off. The pyrotechnics have gone off and it is loud inside the Dragão. Both sides then emerge from the tunnel and here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this evening:.

It has been a positive start for Unai Emery’s Aston Villa out in Belgium as they lead Club Brugge 3-1 at half-time.

According to recent reports, enzo Maresca takes charge of his first Champions League game in charge of Manchester City as they have travelled to Portugal to take on Porto at the Estadio do Dragao. These sides last met during the Champions League group stages during the 2020/21 season. Manchester City won 3-1 at home before the two sides drew 0-0 in this stadium.

Manchester City were busy late on in the transfer window, bringing in both Iliman Ndiaye and Enzo Fernandez as they spent nearly £200m on deadline day alone. They come into tonight’s game off the back of three straight Premier League victories to kick off the Maresca era. Maresca has limited Champions League experience as a manager, which came with Chelsea last season. Manchester City have won their opening game of a Champions League campaign in six of the last seven seasons but this will be the first time since 2015/16 that Manchester City embark on a Champions League campaign without Pep Guardiola at the helm.

Sources indicate that “It is a hard place to come [Porto],” said Maresca. “They have started really well. In the last 14/15 games in Europe they lost just one, that indicates a difficult place to come, but we will try our best and try to win the game. It is a very, very good team. They have different players, but in terms of the team it is very clear in the way they play. They are aggressive without the ball and on the ball, they have a clear style. But we will try our best and try to win the game. The ambition is the same; try to be ourselves and to win games and then we will see.”.

According to recent reports, porto, managed by Francesco Farioli, have won every league game so far this season and already sit four points clear at the summit of Liga Portugal. Farioli takes charge of his first game as a manger in the Champions League and the club make their return to the elite European competition after two seasons away.

In a recent development, “We are going to face one of the substantial favourites to win the competition,” Farioli remarked. “It will be a game that will demand that we be at our best, and we know that whenever we step onto the Dragão pitch, something special can happen. I am happy to be in the Champions League for the first time at 37 years old. This will be my first game, but we approach every game with the same attention to detail and the same focus. It is easy for the players to be motivated tomorrow [tonight]. But the key will be our strategy and our ability to execute it, individually and collectively.”.

Recent findings suggest that porto were in the Europa League last season, making it to the quarter-finals, where they were knocked out by Nottingham Forest 2-1 on aggregate. The omens would not appear to be on Porto’s side tonight; they have only won two of their last 16 games against English opposition in major European competition.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Il tifo organizzato conferma la presenza il 6 dicembre e precisano che non sarà un rientro definitivo.

Così il Tifo Organizzato, tramite un comunicato pubblicato sull'account Instagram.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

A dicembre abbiamo deciso di regalarci un mese intero di Lazio.

Un anno fa questa sarebbe stata la normalità per il popolo bianco celeste ma purtroppo, un presidente tiranno e la sua pletora di tifosi giallorossi, ci hanno costretto a quell’estremo atto di amore che ci ha portato lontano da casa nostra.

In questi lunghi mesi di lontananza abbiamo capito quanto il consenso di questa protesta poggi su basi molto solide perchè ha continuato ad avere dalla sua parte un popolo che ha liberamente scelto di appoggiarla, di contro i vertici di questa società non hanno fatto assolutamente nulla per riavvicinare la tifoseria continuando ad andare nella direzione esattamente opposta ed il popolo laziale ha continuato a scegliere da che parte stare.

Poche eccezioni si sono distinte, tra tutti sicuramente ci sono mister Gattuso, che più volte ha ribadito di capire ed accettare la nostra decisione esprimendo però il “sogno” di vedere lo Stadio Olimpico pieno della sua gente, e la sua squadra (plasmata ad immagine e somiglianza del mister) che ad ogni trasferta è venuta sotto il settore ospite a prendersi il meritato applauso e sappiamo che ci sono vicini!

Per lui, per la squadra, ma soprattutto per tutti quei bambini e tifosi che hanno aderito alla protesta allontanandosi dallo stadio, a quelli che non sono riusciti ad acquistare il biglietto per il derby ed a tutti i laziali che soffrono lontano dalla propria amata Lazio, abbiamo deciso rendere omaggio entrando il 6 dicembre alla partita Lazio-Atalanta.

Caricheremo così anche i ragazzi prima della stracittadina dando un assaggio dell’ambiente che troveranno il 13 dicembre, dimostrando di essere sempre al loro fianco, perché se lo meritano!

Negli scorsi anni siamo andati ad incitarli a Formello ma ormai quel centro sportivo non lo sentiamo più “casa nostra”, sono state fatte molte amichevoli ed il signor Lotito ha pensato bene di farle a porte chiuse per paura della contestazione, ha fatto chiudere la squadra dentro un bunker fregandosene di tutti quei tifosi che avrebbero voluto vedere ed incitare quei ragazzi che oggi ci stanno regalando grandi soddisfazioni.

Non ne facciamo una questione economica, la sortita del pack scontato per tre partite non ha avuto gli effetti desiderati dall’ufficio marketing, la nostra passione non si compra con gli sconti, la nostra fede non è un prodotto da supermercato, scegliamo noi quando entrare, riprovateci ...sarete più fortunati!

Questo non vuol dire bloccare la contestazione, che per questa partita continuerà dentro lo stadio, o erroneamente pensare che si rientri definitivamente, e’ solo l’ennesima prova di unità e compattezza di un popolo contro un despota.

La protesta proseguirà con le stesse modalità di inizio anno, si continuerà a presenziare solo in trasferta ed ai derby e poi, se e quando lo vogliamo tutti noi, sceglieremo (forse) qualche altra giornata di lazialità.

Non si tratta di un passo indietro, altri lo debbono fare, ad iniziare dal tifoso romanista che occupa la sedia del responsabile della comunicazione (al derby come si comporterà!? Tiferà con cuore o continuerà a pensare al portafogli?) noi restiamo fermi sulle nostre posizioni che restano le stesse e non sono minimamente condizionate dall’ottima partenza e dalla meritata posizione in classifica.

Il nostro giudizio completamente negativo su comportamenti del signor Lotito, della gestione vergognosa ed approssimativa della prima società della Capitale, ci fanno restare fermi nella convinzione che un cambio sia urgente per stare al passo con quel mondo del calcio che viaggia ad una velocità tripla rispetto alla nostra Lazio, è doveroso nei confronti di un popolo che vive quotidianamente questo immenso amore e che invece si trova costretto a vivere in un incubo fatto di pressappochismo e botte di fortuna.

In a recent development, come già detto quando abbiamo deciso di non abbonarci e di seguire la Lazio solo in trasferta, anche questa volta chi vuole restare fuori è libero di farlo, chi invece vuole seguirci si prepari a vivere con noi 90 minuti di puro amore! Portate i bambini, mettetegli una bandiera in mano ed una sciarpa al collo e ditegli che per Natale ci regaliamo tutti un dicembre da laziali con quattro partite che ci riossigeneranno fino al derby di ritorno!

Messa da parte l'innovativa esperienza del FIFA U-15 World Cup & Festival con un dodicesimo posto, dal 27 al 29 novembre si disputerà a Novarello il tradizionale Torneo di Natale.

Il ct Enrico Battisti ha convocato 66 calciatori classe 2012, da suddividere in tre squadre di pari numero (Selezione A, Selezione B e Selezione C) che si affronteranno in un triangolare all’italiana.

L'unico ragazzo sotto quota è l'attaccante figlio d'arte Alessandro Criscito (Genoa), presente alla pari del fratello Alfredo.

By LEWIS STEELE, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 12:32 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 18:17 EST, 20 November 2026.

Jack Grealish has been offered an olive branch by Everton boss David Moyes and mentioned the sanctioned star is available for selection this weekend.

It has been revealed that the Manchester City loanee was punished by the club for failing to report to training sessions and missed several matches. He has not featured for four games: one because of illness, then a ‘breach of club discipline’ and a lack of fitness thereafter.

But Grealish will be considered for the squad when the in-form Toffees travel to Brentford on Monday night.

Moyes noted: ‘He has served his punishment and we will treat him as we were treating him before.

‘We will get on with things. The team is going really well at the moment and what I don’t want to do is turn it into a Jack story because it shouldn’t be.’.

In a recent development, pushed if that suggests he will not play on Monday night, Moyes replied: ‘He could easily. He is back in the squad, he is a good player. Who knows?’.

Jack Grealish is available for Everton again after serving his punishment and regaining fitness.

Everton have won their last three games and go into Monday’s match sixth in the table.

Asked what Grealish can offer, the boss added: ‘Jack can offer us a lot. I want more from him, I want him to show more than he has done. I want him to give me more assists, goals.

In a recent development, ‘But there's lots of things about him which we need and he's good at retaining the ball, giving us good possession, carrying. So we hope that he can get back to those levels and give us what we need.

‘I think this time last year he was probably sitting on five or six assists so we're hoping to get that.’.

Grealish's social media apology came after he featured in a behind-closed-doors match during the international break.

'Nice to be back out there with the boys today after a few good days training!' Grealish wrote. 'I want to apologise to the fans (and) everyone at the club for not being able to help the team the last few weeks.

It has been revealed that A presentation from Blues past and present. 🤝Leon Osman and James Tarkowski surprise David Moyes with a memento as he sets a new record for games managed for Everton Football Club (593). 💙 pic.twitter.com/tzFuGeUhFW.

'I love playing for this club (and) can't wait to be back playing in front of you guys in an Everton shirt.

'See you all soon (blue heart)'.

At the start of his press conference Moyes was presented with a framed memento of his time in charge by defender James Tarkowski and former player Leon Osman after he set a upcoming club record of 593 games in the hotseat.

Moyes said: 'It’s something that I’m really thrilled about but, if I’m being honest, it’s not something I really think about. I understand I’ve suddenly become the manager who’s had more games at Everton than anybody before and that’s a real honour and privilege to be put in that position.'.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

L’ex centrocampista della Lazio si allena già con il pallone e, dopo l’intervento, vuole tornare al cento per cento.

It has been revealed that matias Vecino si prepara a tornare in campo dopo l’intervento e alcuni mesi lontano dal calcio giocato. L’ex centrocampista di Lazio e Inter, che ha risolto il contratto con il Celta Vigo, racconta di stare recuperando e indica metà dicembre come il momento in cui conta di essere pronto. A Gianlucadimarzio.com ha detto: «Sto bene, sto recuperando. Mi sto preparando per il ritorno in campo».

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Recent findings suggest that vecino ha ricordato le difficoltà incontrate all’inizio del percorso. Pur sapendo che l’operazione sarebbe stata abbastanza semplice, era consapevole che il recupero avrebbe richiesto tempo: «All'inizio è stato un po' più difficile, affrontare un intervento non è mai semplice. Sapevo che si trattava di un'operazione abbastanza semplice, ma che sarebbero serviti un paio di mesi per recuperare».

Recent findings suggest that il centrocampista è tornato a Roma con la famiglia e prosegue il lavoro insieme al suo staff. «Siamo tornati a Roma con la mia famiglia, sto facendo un bel lavoro con il mio staff. Mi sto preparando», ha spiegato. Il suo obiettivo resta riprendere a giocare, seguendo passo dopo passo il percorso di recupero.

Il classe ’91 ha indicato anche quando pensa di poter essere pronto: «Per metà dicembre sarò pronto. Sono molto ansioso di tornare, sto già lavorando sul campo con il pallone e tutto procede per il verso giusto. Poi vedremo quali opportunità potranno presentarsi».

Una volta recuperata la condizione, Vecino vorrebbe tornare in Serie A. Conosce il campionato italiano, nel quale ha giocato con Inter e Lazio, ma non intende limitare la scelta a questa possibilità. Negli ultimi mesi della scorsa stagione ha vestito la maglia del Celta Vigo.

It has been revealed that «Sarebbe bello tornare in Serie A perché è un campionato che conosco e nel quale mi conoscono. Vedremo quello che succederà», ha dichiarato. Ha poi aggiunto: «Sono aperto anche ad altre opzioni. Dipende dalle possibilità che capiteranno».

It has been revealed that prima di valutare le occasioni che si presenteranno, il centrocampista vuole completare il recupero: «L'importante è stare bene, continuare a recuperare e tornare al cento per cento. Mi manca poco per raggiungere la migliore condizione, poi vedremo». La voglia di rimettersi in gioco passa dunque dal ritorno alla piena forma.

Nel 2006 il Frosinone scriveva una delle pagine più importanti della propria storia, conquistando per la prima volta la promozione in Serie B. Un traguardo che ha segnato l’inizio di un percorso di crescita, ambizione e identità, destinato a portare il club fino alla Serie A e agli ultimi ottimi risultati di questa stagione con Alvini in panchina.

Per l'occasione, al Dream Cinema di Frosinone, i giallazzurri hanno celebrato la ricorrenza presentando la quarta maglia che verrà indossata contro il Parma. La divisa celebrativa riprende l'azzurro originario del Frosinone arricchito da inserti bianchi e gialli, richiamando direttamente l'identità storica della società. Un omaggio scelto per legare le radici del percorso giallazzurro al presente della squadra.

Durante la serata, il presidente Maurizio Stirpe è intervenuto sul palco per ripercorrere i venticinque anni alla guida del club e il valore simbolico di quella prima storica promozione in cadetteria: "È una bella cosa celebrare questi vent'anni con questa maglia che è stata scelta non a caso, perché porta l'azzurro originale dei colori del Frosinone, come il giallo canarino della prima squadra è il colore originale della nostra maglia. Per questo abbiamo voluto collegare la presentazione di questa quarta maglia ai vent'anni che sono passati, anche abbastanza in fretta. Questo è il venticinquesimo anno che sono alla guida del club e all'epoca quella promozione ha costituito il punto di arrivo e il punto di partenza di un nuovo ciclo: partivamo dalla C2, molto in fretta siamo riusciti a colmare il gap e ad arrivare per la prima volta in Serie B, e da lì è incominciata tutta un'altra storia", le parole riportate da tuttofrosinone.com.

Published: 11:24 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 18:21 EST, 20 November 2026.

Chelsea have been slapped with a significant £150,000 fine by the Football Association for their fans’ behaviour during an FA Cup away tie at Charlton Athletic more than ten months ago.

It was alleged that in the 56th minute, the visiting supporters at the Valley sang ‘f*** the Pope and the IRA’. A charge followed, and Chelsea were hit with their fine, along with being given an action plan to follow and a formal warning as to their future conduct.

According to recent reports, chelsea tried to appeal being fined £150,000 for the sectarian chanting. They wanted it either removed completely, or at least substantially reduced.

It has been revealed that the club attempted to argue that it was excessive despite admitting that approximately 2,500 of their fans may have taken part in the offensive singing. They also noted how Millwall were previously not fined for the same chant occurring.

Their appeal was dismissed and the full scale of their punishment was upheld.

In a statement, Chelsea said of the chanting: ‘We unequivocally condemn this behaviour. Sectarian abuse – chanting that creates division targeted towards a particular religious or political group – and discriminatory language of any kind has no place in our football club.

Chelsea have been hit with a £150,000 fine for their fans’ behaviour during an FA Cup away tie at Charlton Athletic back in January.

Xabi Alonso insists his Chelsea stars will show they are not 'soft' after Leeds United rubbed in how often they have bullied their opponents in a video uploaded to their social media.

Leeds produced a compilation of clips of their players leaving crunching challenges in on their Chelsea counterparts and capitalising on mistakes made down the years.

Daniel Farke's side have won more duels than any other club in the Premier League this season, and Alonso's team crumbled when visiting Sunderland before the international break. That was a game in which Levi Colwill and Co were bullied by Brian Brobbey. Colwill was hooked at half-time in that 1-0 loss at the Stadium of Light.

Industry observers note that dominic Calvert-Lewin may now be relishing testing Chelsea at Stamford Bridge, but Alonso noted when asked about being seen as weak: 'We focus on not being soft and being competitive. That's our goal. We have played once this year (a 6-3 win for Chelsea in the Carabao Cup). We will play twice more (in the league). We are ready for that. I like that. We will show that.'.

Calvert-Lewin shares similar attributes to Brobbey in that he is a traditional centre forward who will challenge Chelsea's centre backs.

Industry observers note that 'It¿s quite common in the Premier League that they have a good No 9,' Alonso stated. 'Calvert-Lewin is doing well. He played with England. But it is up to us, how we defend, how we compete in those situations, how we attack the last line, how we attack their defenders. The preparation has, as always, we think been good. We are ready.'.

Asked if defenders have forgotten how to face such strikers, Alonso added: 'Forgotten? No, no, no, I don't think forgotten. But it's demanding to play against No 9s. They have good movement in the box, out the box. This is the demand. You can ask the full-backs, they have to play against great wingers in one v one situations. But I don't think it's been forgotten. But it's good they are back, these type of players.'.

In a recent development, only Tottenham have made more changes to their line-up than Chelsea this season, adding to the suggestion that Alonso is still searching for his preferred style of play. Some have been forced on the Spaniard because of their habit for picking up injuries despite playing only once a week.

'Once you have the whole menu, you can select what you like and I know what I like from the menu,' Alonso said. 'I would like to have more options with the whole squad available but that's something that's difficult to have during the season. I am sure we will get close to that.

'It (the injuries) is a concern. Sometimes you can analyse them and find a reason but sometimes it is difficult to find a reason.'.

Sources indicate that ‘Such behaviour only serves to cause hurt to others and does not represent the values we hold as a club. We want to create a safe and inclusive environment for all, and we have a shared responsibility in delivering this.’.

It has been revealed that they added: ‘We understand that further incidents risk additional sanctions against the club and are doing everything we can to inform and educate supporters, as well as develop our existing initiatives to prevent, detect and respond to discrimination in future. We know Chelsea fans do not want to see any form of discrimination in our game, and we ask for their support in fostering a welcoming environment at Chelsea matches going forward.’.

On the pitch, Chelsea will go into their Saturday clash against Leeds United without star striker Joao Pedro, who has yet to return to training.

It has been revealed that since the Brazilian was sidelined, Chelsea have won only one of their three Premier League games played, beating a beleaguered Manchester United under Michael Carrick. Otherwise, they have lost to Tottenham Hotspur and Sunderland without scoring.

Joao Pedro is still nursing a thigh problem, and has not yet made it outside with his team-mates as Leeds visit Stamford Bridge on Saturday. Chelsea will, however, have Moises Caicedo available after his injury scare during the international break with Ecuador.

In a recent development, ‘He's not fit yet to train with the team, so we need to wait a bit longer,’ Alonso confirmed on Joao Pedro. He’s not going to be available for Leeds. We need to see game by game how he's feeling. So far we have tried different options and we need to keep trying.’.

Chelsea will have Emiliano Martinez available after recovering from his broken jaw suffered at Everton on October 17. The goalkeeper required surgery following his collision with Jarrad Branthwaite. Alonso confirmed he no longer needs to wear a mask, having been training without it, and the 34-year-old Argentinian could be in line for his first club appearance since his injury.

Sources indicate that nonostante abbia dato l'addio dall'estate, Rafael Leao rimane comunque un argomento di attualità tra chi commenta le vicende del Milan. O un termine di paragone, come per esempio nel caso di un commento di Paolo Di Canio, che a Sky Sport ha definito l'attuale rossonero Diego Moreira valere "quattro volte Leao per la serietà, per l'incisività, per la qualità tecnica nella condivisione con i compagni e l'empatia".

In soccorso di Di Canio arriva anche Fabio Caressa. Il noto volto di Sky Sport ha pubblicato un video sul proprio canale YouTube, tornando sul tema: "Di Canio ha detto una cosa importante: Moreira è molto più forte di Leao nelle ultime stagioni. Non c'è proprio paragone come impegno, come caratteristiche, come freschezza e anche come capacità di essere decisivo: acquisto straordinario, secondo me, veramente mi sta piacendo tantissimo. Modric lo conosciamo: non è un caso che Rabiot sia nei primi numeri della Serie A per palle ricevute in verticale sul lungo. È così perché c'è Modric che gliela mette, sennò sarebbe più difficile".

Quindi Caressa ha speso parole anche per la crescita globale della squadra di Amorim: "Il Milan è forte: quando gioca con dodici-tredici giocatori è fortissimo. Ha dei giocatori che fanno le fiamme. Moreira fa le fiamme: domenica ha fatto due o tre cose Moreira che sembrano facili, ma passaggio in controtempo di piatto per liberare l'uomo, passaggio in verticale per costruire il contropiede, tenere palla e darla al momento giusto. Moreira è un giocatore superiore".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Do your talking on the pitch, as the old adage goes, and Alexis Mac Allister emphatically did just that as Liverpool came from behind to thrillingly win their first Champions League tie under new head coach Andoni Iraola in what was his debut at this level.

In a recent development, on the eve of this encounter, against a strong Atlético Madrid, one of the clubs who have recently tried to sign him, Mac Allister had spoken of his sadness. Sadness that, unlike fellow midfielders Dominik Szoboszlai – Liverpool’s other scorer here – and Ryan Gravenberch, he had not been offered and signed a new contract.

Industry observers note that so, earn it. And many more goals – and overall performances like this – there is no doubt the Argentinian will have a deal placed in front of him. He scored with an arresting second-half shot, which proved to be the winner, and the smile across his face said it all. Not so sad now as he was later substituted to a standing ovation with Gravenberch taking his place.

The goal came early in the second half, with Iraola attributing that to adjusting his tactics after being flummoxed by Atlético’s back five and packed midfield in a first half when Liverpool were second best.

Recent findings suggest that mac Allister was heavily involved through the build-up, eventually picking out Rio Ngumoha on the left whose shot was blocked and pinballed around. It dropped to Mac Allister, 20 yards out, and he hit the kind of unerring drive that gives the goalkeeper no chance. And so it proved. Boom. And Anfield was bouncing.

In a recent development, mac Allister FIRES Liverpool into the lead at Anfield! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/KGOvuAEU4W.

There are certainly signs under Iraola, and following a difficult last campaign, that Mac Allister is beginning to rediscover the form he showed during his first two seasons at Liverpool. Time and again the 27-year-old made vital interventions, showed aggression and walked the tightrope of a harsh early yellow card. He dovetailed with Szoboszlai and that might be a concern for Gravenberch – watched by the Netherlands’ new head coach Xavi Hernández – if Iraola persists with this approach.

Although Mac Allister has two years left on his current deal, the last thing Liverpool need is yet another attention-sapping contract saga, even if he is not the same scale of player as Mohamed Salah or Trent Alexander-Arnold.

For Iraola, after three Premier League games, comprising two draws and a victory over newly-promoted Ipswich Town, this will hopefully be lift off. A big European night at Anfield and coming from behind to beat one of the continent’s heavyweights.

“I loved it,” Iraola remarked, before castigating himself for misreading the way Atlético would line up. And what of Mac Allister’s riposte? There was a smile from Iraola before the Spaniard’s usual diplomacy kicked in as he talked about a “lovely, lovely goal” and how good it was for his midfielders to contribute.

Liverpool had to fight for it and what will have satisfied Iraola is that the defence, which has come under such scrutiny, held out. Even so, there are still serious concerns over the suitability of Milos Kerkez at left-back – who was badly at fault for Atlético’s goal – although the robust Ronald Araújo highlighted he can be a strong and versatile option on the other flank. The Uruguayan, signed on loan from Barcelona, is such a presence in both penalty areas and has the capacity to gain cult status.

Sources indicate that as does £123m signing from Paris St-Germain Bradley Barcola, who should have scored – once, certainly, possibly twice – and possesses astonishing pace that will undoubtedly lead to goals. There are also encouraging signs that his presence could enliven Florian Wirtz. Barcola eventually also went off, but thankfully it was only to cramp.

According to recent reports, there was a collective intake of breath across the Kop when Marcos Llorente was played through and bore down on them to give Atlético the lead. There was a desperate hope that he had strayed offside. There was then a realisation that Kerkez had, however, played him on with an appalling lack of awareness. Llorente beat Alisson.

Industry observers note that it owed much to a wonderful shimmy, deceiving Szoboszlai in centre field, by Julián Alvarez before he smartly threaded the ball through, and Mac Allister’s international team-mate almost doubled Atlético’s advantage soon after. Only to be denied by Alisson.

Industry observers note that llorente breaks the deadlock! 🔥That's now FIVE Champions League goals for the Atletico man against Liverpool at Anfield 🤯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Rxp4zurfpc.

It has been revealed that we knew, we feared it would be Llorente who scored. Remarkably, he has now half of his 10 goals in this competition against Liverpool. Indeed, he named his dog Anfield after his extra-time brace knocked Liverpool, then the holders, out in the last 16 in 2020. And Liverpool had made a dog’s dinner of defending this time.

Recent findings suggest that this is a different Atlético. A far less defensive, far more expansive Atlético. In years gone by, once they were 1-0 it was game over under Diego Simeone. But these days they try and play more and that gives their opponents a chance. And so it proved.

Atlético goalkeeper Jan Oblak did well to deny Barcola, with his trailing foot, before Wirtz won the ball back and found Szoboszlai who eventually ended the movement. It owed much, however, to a clever backheel to pick out the midfielder who finished low into the corner. Who executed that backheel? That would be Araújo.

Szoboszlai slots home after a brilliant flick from Araujo! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UrHQTwtgsY.

Barcola should have scored, sent clear by Wirtz in a brilliant, sweeping counter-attack, before Mac Allister did.

Industry observers note that the question now was whether Liverpool would show the resilience to see through the result. As Iraola made changes, they answered that with a resounding yes, which will have pleased him as much as the result, as much as the comeback, as much as Mac Allister’s stunning response.

It has been revealed that “I was enjoying it [the Anfield crowd]. They [Atletico Madrid] are a very good team. Technically, in the middle, lovely players. It is not easy to press those players as they have quality. They have been playing together forever. We find another comeback after Nottingham Forest, after Newcastle. We still have this thing to improve in the beginning of the games, but I am happy as we have shown some character. This is the Champions League, you do not have easy games.”.

"You can see he's football mad." ⚽Steven Gerrard on Andoni Iraola's passion and the impact he's making at Liverpool 👏🎙️ @laura_woodsy | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/M3qKhxt8HE.

Just 60 seconds remain at Anfield.

There will be five added minutes.

In a recent development, liverpool think they have sealed it through Frimpong but the offside flag has gone up. First Munoz cuts onto his right and has a shot saved by Oblak. The ball falls to Frimpong, who slots home but he was clearly offside when Munoz took the initial shot.

Kerkez is currently down with cramp and his night is done. He will be replaced by Tsimikas and Liverpool will make their final change at the same time. Koumas comes on for Isak.

The corner is flicked on by Hjulmand but ends up coming to nothing.

It isn’t the headline making performance, by any means, but that shouldn’t dilute the importance of Ronald Araujo’s contribution for Liverpool tonight and, indeed, against Ipswich last Friday. He’s doing what Liverpool wanted him to, providing versatility and leadership in their back four and - more than anything - quality. He hasn’t put a foot wrong.

In a recent development, atletico win a corner out on the left in front of their travelling supporters. Grimaldo’s outswinger is flicked on by the head of Hancko at the near post but it goes over.

Digeo Simeone is making his final two substitutions of the night as Le Normand and Hjulmad replace Romero and Barrios,.

Atletico bring on David, on loan from Juventus, for Baena.

Sources indicate that we’ll see what happens in the coming weeks and months but there have been glimmers here with Florian Wirtz looking better than he has done with pace to pass to; if it clicks with him, Bradley Barcola & Alexander Isak it could be exciting but one game must be built on. It has been revealed that this is a concern for Liverpool. Barcola has gone down and seems to have some pain in his left calf. Is it cramp or an injury? Ngumoha also heads off.

Diego Simeone most wonder how Atleti are losing a game they were controlling but Liverpool’s speed on the break is proving very good at causing chaos.

The original “This is Anfield” sign has sold at auction for almost £150,000, 10 times more than its guide price.

The sign that hung above the players’ tunnel at Liverpool’s home stadium during the 1970s had been expected to fetch between £10,000 and £15,000 after being put up for auction on Tuesday and Wednesday.

But the “talismanic” piece of football memorabilia ended up being sold by auctioneer Budds for £149,500 to a UK private buyer.

The Argentine is into the final two years of his contract, which runs out in 2028. He arrived at Liverpool in the same summer as fellow midfielders Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai, who have both signed new contracts. Mac Allister was linked with a move away from Liverpool during the summer transfer window and was candid about his contractual situation in the press conference yesterday:.

“I received the news that the club was not in a position to offer me a latest contract which, of course, makes me very, very sad. Everyone can see that I give my 100% for this football club every single day in training and games. Of course, I can have very good games [and] bad games, like everyone, but I always give my best.

“I see Dominik [Szoboszlai] and Ryan [Gravenberch] renewing their contracts and that makes me very happy because they deserve it. At the same time it makes me a little bit sad that I did not get mine. Of course, there is still time. The fans do not need to worry because I will give my 100% until the last day I am here. There were options to leave this summer. I think right now I am in the right club and I have the right mindset to give 100% for this club.”.

When Liverpool won their sixth European Cup in 2019, they lifted it in the Wanda Metropolitano against Tottenham. This season’s Champions League final is in that very stadium and Liverpool’s Champions League campaign starts tonight against the club that plays their home games in that stadium, Atletico Madrid.

“This is going to be a challenge, I hope, all the season because it would mean we continue in all the competitions. In this case, it is not the worst scenario because we played last Friday so we have had I think a good recovery. Sources indicate that liverpool begin their Champions League campaign at home as they host Atletico Madrid at Anfield. These sides met at Anfield on matchday one last season, with Liverpool winning a dramatic game 3-2. Liverpool led 2-0 inside the opening 10 minutes before Atletico came back to level the game at 2-2. Virgil van Dijk then scored in added time to give Liverpool all three points before Atletico boss Diego Simeone was sent off for clashing with the Anfield crowd, resulting in a one-match ban.

Andoni Iraola earned his first win as Liverpool boss on Friday night as they won 2-0 away at Ipswich thanks to a quickfire early double from Alexander Isak. This will be Iraola’s first Champions League match as a manager.

According to recent reports, “I think obviously it is a special night for me,” Iraola said. “Everyone talks [about] the Champions League nights at Anfield and also the first game is against a strong opposition, it is Atletico Madrid. [Diego] Simeone is doing an incredible job as a manager. To be all the years that he has been achieving every season the goals of the club I think is remarkable and definitely it is a major challenge for us. I think I played against him as a player, he was still a player, and I played against his teams when he was a coach and I also coached against him. So, we had a lot of precedent before. Definitely he has much more experience than me in this kind of games but I hope tomorrow we can give him a good game.

According to recent reports, “It is one of the dreams, probably, when you start. It was difficult for me when I started my coaching career seven, eight years ago, to position myself in the position that I am right now, and I hope I can enjoy it. It is a massive responsibility, massive challenge, but I feel privileged to be there in that dugout tomorrow [tonight] and now my thinking is about putting the team together in a position where we can play a good game, win the game and start strong in this Champions League.”.

Atletico Madrid at the moment sit sixth in La Liga and suffered their first defeat on Saturday as they lost 3-0 at Athletic Bilbao. They did reach the semi-finals of the Champions League last season, where they fell to Arsenal 2-1 on aggregate.

“We are coming into a marvellous stadium and there will be a great atmosphere,” Simeone said. “We will have to look good from the start of the game because it will be full on. He [Andoni Iraola] works very well with the team, focusing on the tactical awareness of each player. It takes time to find the right path, but he is growing and improving and he has some very good players.”.

Recent findings suggest that massimiliano Allegri, allenatore del Napoli, ha rilasciato alcune dichiarazioni a Sky Sport, dopo il match contro il Manchester City di Champions League: “Questa partita sia stata importante, questo punto se vinciamo due partite, sarebbe importante per la qualificazione. La partita era difficile, i ragazzi sono stati bravi con l’uscita palla, Ci sono cose che abbiamo fatto bene come la fase di non possesso, li abbiamo rallentati, sono stati bravi. Dispiace, è un pareggio meritato, anche se c’è l’amaro in bocca per la mancata vittoria. Ai ragazzi ho detto che avere coraggio in Europa ci deve essere e va fatto crescere. Poi domenica abbiamo una partita importante che va preparata a livello mentale. Ma quella di questa sera è un buon allenamento. Siamo contenti per il punto, ma possiamo sfruttare alcune occasioni nel primo tempo. I ragazzi sono stati bravi nell’applicazione della partita. perdendo un calciatore straordinario, così come Modric. Restare fino a giugno? Ne parleremo con la società, ma è un ragazzo serio e credo resterà fino a giugno. Nella prima parte di stagione, con più responsabilità mia, abbiamo curato poco la fase difensiva, ma sono segnali che non vanno bene. Il gol lo devi prendere, ma stasera il City ha sudato per farlo, questo è l’atteggiamento giusto, serve la cattiveria giusta che non abbiamo avuto nella prima parte di campionato”.

  • La sentenza di primo grado aveva solo comminato sanzioni disciplinari, poi in appello il ko a tavolino per il Senegal, reo di aver "abbandonato il campo prima della fine prevista della partita senza il permesso dell'arbitro".

It has been revealed that il Senegal torna campione d'Africa. Il Tribunale Arbitrale dello Sport ha infatti riassegnato all'unanimità la contestata Coppa del 2025, ribaltando la decisione che aveva attribuito al Marocco il trofeo a tavolino. Il 17 marzo, la commissione d'appello della Confederazione Africana di Calcio aveva revocato il titolo al Senegal, assegnandolo al Marocco, dopo una finale segnata da incidenti ma comunque terminata.

Recent findings suggest that il Senegal a sua volta aveva presentato ricorso al Tas che, a più di dieci mesi dalla finale, ha ritenendo che l'arbitro non avesse commesso alcun errore nell'ordinare la ripresa del gioco dopo gli incidenti. Il 18 gennaio a Rabat, il Senegal aveva vinto la Coppa d'Africa battendo 1-0 il Marocco dopo i tempi supplementari e il caos, per la contestazione di un rigore assegnato al Marocco nei minuti di recupero.

La sentenza di primo grado aveva solo comminato sanzioni disciplinari, poi in appello il ko a tavolino per il Senegal, reo di aver "abbandonato il campo prima della fine prevista della partita senza il permesso dell'arbitro". La Federcalcio senegalese aveva denunciato "il più sfacciato furto nella storia del nostro sport". Ora il successo al Tas e la Coppa che torna al Senegal. Il Marocco può ancora ricorrere alla Corte federale svizzera, che non si pronuncia sul merito ma interviene sulle questioni procedurali.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Vincenzo Montella, ex allenatore del Milan, ha rilasciato una intervista a La Gazzetta dello Sport, ricordando i suoi tempi in rossonero.

C'è stato il mercato delle cose formali...

Industry observers note that "Io dall'inizio era un po' preoccupato perché c'è questa mania di esternare tutto, quasi pubblicitario più che altro, quindi ero un po' preoccupato. In teoria c'era condivisione, almeno così si palesava, ma non potevo tirarmi indietro quando in realtà non era sempre così. E quindi alcune volte c'erano dei calciatori per cui non ero neanche stato consultato, che arrivavano e che poi dicevano 'È stato condiviso': quando sei lì non puoi dire diversamente. Sicuramente, quando si costruisce una squadra e hai il budget, la prima cosa che fai è: il portiere ce l'avevamo, prendo un centravanti, ci manca il centravanti. Nella scelta di tutto era rimasto il centravanti, con un budget - se non ricordo male - sui quindici-venti milioni. E quindi poi Kalinić... lui sì, l'ho scelto io perché quello era il budget. Quindi la nostra, diciamo, seconda scelta di attaccante fu pagato trentotto milioni, se non ricordo male, che era André Silva, e il primo attaccante fu la metà. E quindi, se non ricordo male, si è creato un equivoco di questo tipo, con tanti cambi, che poi in quella fase non giocavamo neanche male per avere, credo, quindici giocatori nuovi. Avevamo ancora Calhanoglu che non stava bene, che veniva da sei mesi di inattività per squalifica, se non ricordo male: quindi, nel contesto, era in costruzione la squadra; non eravamo in linea con gli obiettivi dello scudetto che erano stati proclamati, ma sicuramente per un processo di crescita eravamo assolutamente in linea".

"All'epoca forse stavamo trattando Aubameyang, se non ricordo male".

Cristiano Ronaldo, si parlava anche di lui: ci credevi?

“No, non credevo: anzi, proprio per nulla".

💡 Key Takeaways

  • La Lega ha infatti pubblicato il bando per l’assegnazione dei diritti audiovisivi della Coppa Italia e della Supercoppa Italiana per il triennio 2027-2030, inserendo due possibili formule alternative per la coppa nazionale.
  • La novità più interessante per il mondo nerazzurro è contenuta nel cosiddetto Format B, che prevede l’allargamento della competizione a 56 squadre e apre alla partecipazione di un numero maggiore di società di Serie C, comprese potenzialmente le seconde squadre dei club di Serie A.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that inter contro Inter U23 in una finale di Coppa Italia? Uno scenario che oggi appare quasi fantascientifico, ma che trova spazio nelle ipotesi di riforma della competizione presentate dalla Lega Serie A.

La Lega ha infatti pubblicato il bando per l’assegnazione dei diritti audiovisivi della Coppa Italia e della Supercoppa Italiana per il triennio 2027-2030, inserendo due possibili formule alternative per la coppa nazionale.

La novità più interessante per il mondo nerazzurro è contenuta nel cosiddetto Format B, che prevede l’allargamento della competizione a 56 squadre e apre alla partecipazione di un numero maggiore di società di Serie C, comprese potenzialmente le seconde squadre dei club di Serie A.

Ma c’è un passaggio particolarmente curioso.

�Le Seconde Squadre non possono incontrare le rispettive Prime Squadre se non in Finale».

Questo significa che, qualora venisse adottata la nuova formula e l’Inter U23 ottenesse il diritto di partecipare, la formazione di Cristian Chivu e la seconda squadra nerazzurra non potrebbero affrontarsi nei turni precedenti alla finale.

Un eventuale incrocio tra le due formazioni sarebbe dunque consentito soltanto nell’atto conclusivo della competizione.

Naturalmente si tratta di una possibilità puramente teorica, che richiederebbe a entrambe le squadre di raggiungere la finale.

Per l’Inter U23, tuttavia, sarebbe un’opportunità importante per confrontarsi anche con avversarie delle categorie superiori.

MONZA, ITALY - FEBRUARY 04: General view inside the dressing room ahead of Coppa Italia match between FC Internazionale and Torino FC at U-Power Stadium on February 04, 2026 in Monza, Italy. (Photo by Mattia Pistoia - Inter/Inter via Getty Images).

Il Format A ripropone sostanzialmente l’attuale struttura della Coppa Italia.

Il Format B, invece, introduce una serie di modifiche significative:.

•⁠ ⁠56 squadre partecipanti: 20 di Serie A, 20 di Serie B e 16 di Serie C. •⁠ ⁠Ingresso delle otto teste di serie ai sedicesimi, anziché agli ottavi di finale. •⁠ ⁠Semifinali in gara unica, eliminando il doppio confronto di andata e ritorno. •⁠ ⁠Possibilità per le seconde squadre di partecipare in base ai criteri previsti. •⁠ ⁠Impossibilità per le seconde squadre di affrontare le rispettive prime squadre prima della finale.

Per le grandi società di Serie A, dunque, cambierebbe anche il percorso verso la conquista del trofeo.

Le otto teste di serie dovrebbero iniziare la competizione un turno prima rispetto a oggi, ma l’eliminazione delle semifinali di andata e ritorno compenserebbe l’impegno supplementare.

Inizialmente, il Format B prevedeva una corsia preferenziale per le seconde squadre delle società di Serie A, indipendentemente dal campionato nel quale militassero.

Secondo quanto riportato da Tuttomercatoweb nella serata del 24 novembre, la Lega Serie A ha successivamente corretto il testo, eliminando questa priorità.

Si sarebbe trattato di un errore materiale nella stesura del documento.

In caso di adozione del nuovo formato, dunque, le sedici società provenienti dalla Serie C verrebbero individuate secondo criteri di merito, senza favorire automaticamente le seconde squadre.

Anche l’Inter U23, quindi, dovrebbe conquistare sul campo il diritto di partecipare alla competizione, secondo i criteri che saranno stabiliti.

La Lega ha infatti presentato entrambe le ipotesi agli operatori televisivi interessati all’acquisto dei diritti per le stagioni 2027/28, 2028/29 e 2029/30.

Le offerte economiche delle emittenti contribuiranno a determinare quale delle due formule verrà adottata.

Il Format B, che comprende più partite e una partecipazione più ampia delle società di Serie C, potrebbe quindi entrare in vigore a partire dalla stagione 2027/28.

E per l’Inter si aprirebbe anche uno scenario davvero particolare: vedere la propria seconda squadra partecipare alla stessa Coppa Italia della prima formazione, con la possibilità di un derby nerazzurro soltanto in finale.

Una prospettiva ancora lontana, ma che per la prima volta trova spazio nelle ipotesi ufficiali della Lega Serie A.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 21:00 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 21:00 EST, 20 November 2026.

It has been revealed that some grounds are beautiful. Some grounds are not so beautiful. Some grounds take you to the heart of the English game. And some leave you feeling like you're on the periphery.

But each of them holds the soul of their community and the hopes and dreams of the thousands of people who make the pilgrimage there every weekend.

It has been revealed that on April 1, 2025, I made the trip to Harrogate Town’s Exercise Stadium and first fulfilled the quest of a lifetime by completing the set of all 92 English Football League grounds for Daily Mail Sport. But then Everton moved away from Goodison Park and into a stunning new stadium on the banks of the River Mersey.

I was one short again but on February 23, 2026, I got back up to 92 by going to Hill Dickinson Stadium to watch Everton versus Manchester United. Then, in November, with York City being promoted (alongside Rochdale, whose ground I had ticked off decades ago), I made the trip to the LNER Stadium to make the 92 whole again.

It has been revealed that I won’t give too much away just yet, but why are grounds like AFC Wimbledon and Exeter City in my top 20? What about Anfield, Old Trafford and Stamford Bridge? Where does Everton’s dazzling latest home rank? Where is the best grub in the Premier League and where did Tyson Fury once threaten to have my jaw broken?

This is my love letter to English football. Read on to find out who comes out on top, where your team ranks and everything else in between – then let me know what you think of my guide to the 92 grounds of England.

Division: Championship Opened: 1993 Capacity: 19,369.

Being banned from The Den is the football equivalent of being banned from your local abattoir.

I’ve been banned from The Den for the last 20 months, in a professional capacity anyway. I could still go in a personal capacity but, on balance, I think I’d rather not.

The Daily Mail has been told that our reporters are not welcome at the club because we had the temerity to report on the horrendous challenge by Millwall goalkeeper Liam Roberts on Crystal Palace’s Jean-Philippe Mateta during the FA Cup tie at Selhurst Park in March last year, which left the French striker requiring 25 stitches in his left ear.

Industry observers note that let’s be honest about this: there are worse places to be banned from. Being banned from The Den is the football equivalent of being banned from your local abattoir. You don’t have to be a racist, misogynistic, homophobic bloke with anger complications and a penchant for tragedy-chanting to feel at home at The Den. But it helps.

And, yes, I know Millwall are trying to rebrand themselves as a ‘family club’ now and the odd Tarquin and Tabitha stray across the county lines from Blackheath and Clapham to keep it real but that just makes The Den experience even worse.

The last time I went as a supporter was 16 years ago to watch Stockport County play there and the walk from South Bermondsey station to the away turnstiles was an eye-opener.

Not that there were any problems: even at Millwall, football has moved on since the 70s. But this still felt deeply dystopian: for their own safety, away fans walk to the ground through a long wire mesh cage that seems to have no end. It felt like embarking on a tour of Jurassic Park: you know that if the fences fail, the dinosaurs are going to take a run at you.

Industry observers note that inside the ground, which is modern and neat and relatively characterless, the level of hatred for visiting supporters feels unusually visceral. It’s loud. I’ll give it that. It’s primeval. It’s unreconstructed, which can be a good thing, too, and it breeds a sense of togetherness.

It has been revealed that if medievalism is your thing, you’re in for a treat. If not, give it a miss.

Division: League One Opened: 2007 Capacity: 30,303.

In a recent development, I know it’s a soft target but I really don’t care much for Stadium MK. Or for MK Dons, for that matter.

According to recent reports, I know it’s a soft target but I really don’t care much for Stadium MK. Or for MK Dons themselves for that matter.

According to recent reports, the club was born under a bad sign when it was jemmied out of Wimbledon and moved to Milton Keynes in 2003 and it has never been able to shake the stigma since. The stadium fits the club.

Recent findings suggest that it is a soulless, faceless, gloomy place. More than that, there is something rather forbidding about it. Its 30,000 capacity is too big for the club it hosts and, apart from the joys of the local KFC and McDonald’s, there is little to recommend in its immediate surrounds. Its black seats lend it a sinister air, too.

In a recent development, it’s the kind of stadium only its mother could love. And it doesn’t have a mother. Unless you want to do the 92, give it a miss.

90. Kassam Stadium, Oxford United.

Division: League One Opened: 2001 Capacity: 12,537.

The empty end kills a lot of the atmosphere, although the Oxford fans are to be commended for the noise they do generate.

I feel ashamed to say it, given that it is my local club, but the best experience I’ve had at the Kassam Stadium was getting my Covid jab there during the pandemic.

When they moved, around the turn of the century, abandoning the chaotic charm of the Manor Ground in Headington and swapping it for an isolated plateau outside the city, they only completed three sides, abandoning the fourth because of rising costs.

A particularly bitter wind blows in off the car park behind one of the goals and, from the main stand – in fact, from every stand – there is a magnificent and uninterrupted view of the Frankie and Benny's in the mini retail park that abuts the ground.

The empty end kills a lot of the atmosphere, too, although the Oxford fans are to be commended for the noise they do generate given they have endured a generation of being stuck here. Firoz Kassam still owns the stadium but not the club. That kind of separation always spells trouble.

Oxford are hoping to move to a new stadium to the north of the city in a couple of years’ time. It can’t come soon enough.

It has been revealed that 89. London Stadium, West Ham United.

Division: Championship Opened: 2012 Capacity: 62,500.

It was a great athletics arena and home to a whole host of golden memories at London 2012 but it’s a dog’s dinner of a football ground.

I don’t even like calling it the London Stadium. It’s the Olympic Stadium, but it suited the David Sullivan-Karren Brady rebrand of the club to give it the capital’s name.

It was a great athletics arena and home to a whole host of golden memories at London 2012 but it’s a dog’s dinner of a football ground. It’s also a monument to much that is wrong with the upper reaches of the English game: a surrender of identity and tradition as collateral damage in the owners’ pursuit of profit.

Recent findings suggest that walking to it, sadly, feels a bit like walking through a wasteland and its odd configuration inside harms the atmosphere even though the fans are right up there with the best in the country. The old stadium at Upton Park was intimate and raucous and intimidating. The London Stadium is nothing like that.

The owners spent a lot of time congratulating themselves on the deal they did to move to the new ground: they’re the archetypes of football owners who know the price of everything and the value of nothing.

88. Hillsborough, Sheffield Wednesday.

Division: League One Opened: 1899 Capacity: 34,835.

It is hard to get past Hillsborough's association with so much death and despair and heartbreak and the betrayal of supporters.

I used to think of Hillsborough as one of the cathedrals of the English game but since the disaster that claimed the lives of 97 Liverpool fans in 1989, it is hard to get past its association with so much death and despair and heartbreak and betrayal of supporters.

I know, obviously, that this would punish Wednesday fans who do not deserve to be punished for something that had nothing to do with them but Hillsborough, and its Leppings Lane End in particular, has such a cursed legacy that part of me thinks it should have been demolished and that the club should have moved elsewhere.

Even in the last couple of years, fans of Newcastle United and Leeds United have reported serious safety concerns in the Leppings Lane End.

I recognise the flaws in my argument about demolishing the stadium, or part of it, and the emotions it provokes on all sides so perhaps it’s just enough to say I’ll never feel the same about the stadium as I once did.

Visiting it now feels like an intrusion.

87. Sixfields, Northampton Town.

Division: League Two Opened: 1994 Capacity: 8,203.

Sixfields is a soulless ground anyway but its issues have been compounded by redevelopment delays and questions about missing money.

Sixfields is a blighted stadium.

It is a soulless ground anyway but its problems have been compounded by redevelopment delays and questions about missing money.

Recent findings suggest that it has the same kind of deracinated feel as so many of the new-build stadia pushed to the peripheries of towns. Its supporters deserve a lot better.

It has been revealed that 86. Broadfield Stadium, Crawley Town.

Division: League Two Opened: 1997 Capacity: 5,907.

If you visit the Broadfield Stadium, I think you might doubt if Crawley are even in League Two.

Not an awful lot to relish about the Broadfield Stadium, to be honest.

Decent fans, of course, just like at every club, but Crawley Town’s home is a bit of a modern monstrosity, next to a roundabout outside town on the A23.

It has been revealed that if you visit the Broadfield Stadium, I think you might doubt if Crawley are even in League Two. I had fun when I visited because I was in the away end with Stockport fans but I’m not in any hurry to go back.

85. Coventry Building Society Arena, Coventry City.

Division: Premier League Opened: 2005 Capacity: 32,609.

Football at the CBS Arena feels like it is in an urban wasteland but it is football, nonetheless.

When it was called the Ricoh Arena, I had no interest in visiting what is now the Coventry Building Society Arena because it felt like a symbol of the callous way in which fans of the club were being treated by SISU, the hedge fund that owned it at the time.

According to recent reports, but SISU sold up in the end and I went along a few years back to see Coventry dismantle Wayne Rooney’s Birmingham City. Then, in the press room beneath the stadium, I watched as my colleague Neil Moxley got into a decent old-fashioned row with Rooney about his stewardship of the Blues.

The atmosphere inside the ground was lively enough, partly because the game was a derby of sorts, but it is a soulless stadium abutting the M6.

It is football in an urban wasteland but it is football, nonetheless, and Doug King, the new owner, has brought with him much better times.

In a recent development, 84. JobServe Community Stadium, Colchester United.

Division: League Two Opened: 2008 Capacity: 10,105.

This stadium on a roundabout on the A12 in the middle of a retail park is rather a bleak place to watch football.

The staff at the club are great, the stewards are friendly, there's plenty of parking, there's a Wendy's next door and the home fans, largely arranged in a stand behind one of the goals, make a superb first of creating an atmosphere.

But this stadium on a roundabout on the A12 in the middle of a retail park is still rather a bleak place to watch football.

It probably didn’t help that I went on a dank March night when a wispy fog lingered in the dim floodlight glare but there was something ethereally gloomy about the JobServe Community Stadium.

The empty corridors and the cavernous suites lent it a slight feel of the Overlook Hotel on the inside. On the outside, the four corners of the stadium are open, which makes for especially bitter nights in the winter.

Home is home and there was still plenty of drama and passion in Colchester’s 1-0 victory over Chesterfield – the match I saw – but it came despite the stadium, not because of it.

It has been revealed that 83. Pallet-Track Bescot Stadium, Walsall.

Division: League Two Opened: 1990 Capacity: 10,863.

The Bescot Stadium was the first of the generation of identikit latest-build arenas I went to and there is not, frankly, much to recommend it apart from the loyalty of the fans.

The Bescot was the first of the generation of identikit new-build arenas I went to and there is not, frankly, much to recommend it apart from the loyalty of the fans.

It’s close to the M6 and it’s a seven-minute walk to Walsall station – so you can get away from it promptly, which some would say is a bonus.

82. Brick Community Stadium, Wigan Athletic.

Division: League One Opened: 1999 Capacity: 25,133.

The name changes are irrelevant to some but they betray a lack of care for the identity of a football club.

I stood on the terraces at Springfield Park as a Stockport fan.

Once again, it will not come as a surprise to learn I preferred it to its successor, the JJB Stadium, which later became the DW Stadium and is now the Brick Community Stadium.

The name changes are irrelevant to some but they betray a lack of care for the identity of a football club.

There were some great days and nights there when Wigan were promoted to the Premier League and I remember, in particular, the heady feeling of watching Wigan’s first home game in the top flight, against Jose Mourinho’s Chelsea in 2005.

The limelight has moved away again now and Wigan are left with a stadium that is perfectly adequate and also perfectly unremarkable.

81. The Croud Meadow, Shrewsbury Town.

Division: League Two Opened: 2007 Capacity: 9,875.

Abutted by a McDonald’s and a TK Maxx on the outer fringes of the town, it feels like a disembodied place, separated from its community, functional but uninspired.

Gay Meadow, the former home of Shrewsbury Town, was one of the best grounds in our top four divisions.

It might have flooded now and again because of its position on the banks of the River Severn but it was a fine old ground and the tradition of a boatman taking to a coracle to fish wayward shots that cleared the roof of the stand out of the river was one of the most cherished peculiarities in our game.

The Croud Meadow is altogether more prosaic. Abutted by a McDonald’s and a TK Maxx on the outer fringes of the town, it feels like a disembodied place, separated from its community, functional but uninspired.

80. Select Car Leasing Stadium, Reading.

Division: League One Opened: 1998 Capacity: 24,376.

I was persona non grata for a while at the Select Car Leasing Stadium when I took exception to Reading taking out two Chelsea goalkeepers in one match back in 2006.

I was persona non grata for a while at the Select Car Leasing Stadium when I took exception to Reading taking out two Chelsea goalkeepers in one match back in 2006, when Steve Coppell and Wally Downes were in charge at the Madejski Stadium.

People called it the Mad Stad back then and I remember Neil Warnock telling me about being chased to his car outside the main entrance when he was manager of Sheffield United.

And Wally took a swing at me at a Football Writers’ Association dinner a couple of years later.

Anyway, I’ve made up with Stephen Hunt, who was one of the players involved in the tumult against Chelsea, and with Downes since then.

Even if the Mad Stad doesn’t have an awful lot of personality, I have only respect for the Reading fans who endured so much under the ownership of Dai Yongge and fought for their club.

Recent findings suggest that 79. Pride Park Stadium, Derby County.

Division: Championship Opened: 1997 Capacity: 32,956.

Too many of the modern bowls have lost character because the fans just merge into one.

Pride Park is the standard-bearer, sadly, for what is lacking in many of the fresh generation of English football stadia.

English football grounds should be about the North Bank and the Stretford End and the Kop and the Gallowgate End and the Shelf.

They’re supposed to be about defined areas that give a stadium character and personality and even rivalry among home fans about who sings loudest.

Too many of the modern bowls have lost that character because the fans just merge into one.

This is not a criticism of Derby County fans in any way. They still make plenty of noise inside their stadium but the place is not a patch on the Baseball Ground, which witnessed so many momentous days and nights.

Pride Park is bland and featureless, a symbol of its team’s current struggle for identity as it languishes near the foot of the Championship.

According to recent reports, 78. Swansea.com Stadium, Swansea City.

Division: Championship Opened: 2003 Capacity: 20,996.

The Swansea.com Stadium lacks character but is a tight ground where the fans can still generate a rousing atmosphere if their team’s displays allow it.

My in-laws used to live in Swansea and when I wasn’t out walking to Worm’s Head at Rhossili or enjoying the delights of Mumbles and the Wales Coast Path, I’d make the occasional pilgrimage to what was left of the Vetch Field.

It has been revealed that I stood in the away end there with Manchester United fans in the early 80s but when I visited later in my life, the Vetch was locked up and derelict. If you peered through the gates, you could see small trees and shrubs growing on the pitch.

The Swansea.com Stadium lacks the same character, obviously, but it is a tight ground where the fans can still generate a rousing atmosphere if their team’s displays allow it.

I did a phone interview with Mike Tyson from the press box here a couple of hours before a game once. I couldn’t hear him very well because of various announcements being made over the loud-speaker system and soon, his tone became rather impatient but still, a conversation with Mike Tyson in the press box at Swansea is not easily forgotten.

Burton’s a fine club with a distinguished non-League history that can boast Neil Warnock and Nigel Clough as former managers and which has nailed down its place in the Football League.
